- mr president, we are here again to discuss gmos. today, the question of the transfrontier movement of these goods is unlike any other. will there be any discussion tomorrow of legislation on cases of accidental release, unintentional risks in the field of gmos? i'm a caricature, of course. but this is only the beginning of a long series of debates which, let us admit, sometimes take on a surreal tone. we agree with the spirit of the proposal for a regulation on the requirements of the cartagena protocol, but we would like to point out the paradoxical aspect of the process. the agreement is supposed to guarantee the necessary legal framework for transboundary movements of gmos, but at the same time it recognises the contradictory notion of unintentional transboundary movements. it is clear that such measures are a means of dealing with situations of scientific uncertainty, something which the countries of the south cannot afford to do as calmly as we can. in fact, when we voted last july on setting the threshold for accidental contamination of gmos at 0.5% or 1%, did we show any serenity? in writing. - in 1999, the tampere summit set 2004 as the deadline for implementing the common asylum policy. it is clear that the objective set by the fifteen is very difficult to achieve. the texts and reports pile up, each time proposing a new step in the harmonization of the right of asylum, but in the end no consensus, no progress! only two projects have been approved so far, and again, by word of mouth. even the seville summit, which was supposed to be a major event in the fight against illegal immigration, was a failure. the member states of the european union have only been able to agree on the lowest common denominator: not to punish the countries of illegal immigration. the european files on the common asylum and immigration policy have become bogged down, whether it is the definition of refugee status, asylum policy, family reunification or the admission of foreign workers in certain economic and social sectors. why are you stuck ? simply because it is a matter of national competence: the right of every country to manage its own migration flows and to implement its own immigration policy. brussels wants to make everything a community, but it is difficult for each state to lose a part of its sovereignty. in writing. - in the wake of the september 11 attacks, the council called on the commission to examine urgently the relationship between the maintenance of internal security and compliance with international obligations in the field of asylum. it has done so in a disappointing way, dealing with only one question: how to exclude terrorists and other criminals from the right of asylum? it's seeing the problem through the small end of the lens. but there is another, much more serious question which the commission document omits entirely: what would happen if a whole section of the population of a third country sought asylum in one or more member states because they were at risk of oppression in their own country? since 1950, we've changed our world. the geneva convention was designed to protect persecuted individuals. today, with globalisation and the ease of transport, we must consider that its application will one day be demanded by entire populations, by millions of refugees who would destabilise our countries. that is the main question today. governments have a duty to respond by complementing existing rules with alternative protections to traditional asylum.
in writing. - at the moment of taking stock, after five years of implementation of the european employment strategy, and before the final adoption of the employment guidelines for 2003, it is important to remember that unemployment remains a scourge, and that it is the main cause of social exclusion. this is why several requirements are necessary: to ask the commission to analyse the causes of the low economic growth in the union and to come forward with proposals to encourage real and significant growth to increase the supply of jobs. at the methodological level, the aim is to strengthen the role of national parliaments in the process of drawing up national action plans, to give the european parliament a role, in the framework of the codecision procedure, in employment matters covered by the open method of coordination, and to involve the social partners more closely. in the context of the reform of the structural funds, the commission has proposed that the community should provide financial support for the development of the structural funds, in particular through the structural funds, in order to help the regions to develop their economies and to contribute to the development of the regions. better integration of legal immigrants into the labour market must also be considered.

- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, although i agreed with mr mayer's report, i was somewhat surprised by the question put to the commission, since the time allotted to it to carry out these studies was not very long. i am also convinced that the transition from community exhaustion of trade marks to international exhaustion is likely to be both economically harmful and legally awkward. neither nera nor the economist intelligence unit have shown that the international duty drawback system has a significant effect on consumer prices in the long term. the consumer would not be the beneficiary of such a change and i want to see this as evidenced by the recent article published by the evening standard on 4 september last, revealing that tesco, known for its position in favour of the international duty-exhaustion regime, has not given the consumer a substantial price advantage achieved in parallel importation. moreover, if we want to adopt international exhaustion, we will have to amend not only the 1988 directive but also the 1993 regulation establishing the community trade mark and enshrining the community exhaustion rule. it would be inconceivable that international exhaustion applied to the national trade mark while the community trade mark was not. such a solution would certainly lead to the disappearance of national trade marks, which are dear to the states and which are needed by businesses, especially small and medium-sized ones, in the frequent cases where protection throughout the union appears to them to be unnecessary and costly. more than ever before, in a context of intensified globalisation, we must affirm the economic importance of the european union by integrating the single market and promoting our creativity. neither the united states nor japan has adopted international brand exhaustion. if the european union unilaterally decided to move to this legal regime, it would introduce a distortion of competition between the european union and third countries. brand protection is vital for the european economy and consumer safety. the brand is the guarantee of the authenticity and quality of a product. in addition, the current regime provides better protection against counterfeiting, as parallel imports pose a major risk as they use the same channels as pirated and counterfeit products. mr mayer asked a question, but i have a question of my own which seems to me to be of the utmost importance: why has the european union not yet signed the madrid protocol, which would provide an integrated, effective, comprehensive and transparent system of trademark protection? i therefore warmly urge the european union to sign this protocol.

the cotonou agreement promising a new participatory approach, the time has come to innovate. a broad public debate alongside open and transparent negotiations would be a good start. the issue of these negotiations has a major impact on the existing debate on the relationship between trade and development. the development dimension is becoming increasingly important in our trade policy, commissioner lamy told us. we are still concerned that development is thus increasingly reduced to a mere dimension added to trade liberalisation, when it is determined policies that it needs. the question of the merits of the opening of markets as such cannot be avoided. it does not, for example, eliminate the deterioration of the terms of trade for the poor countries, which is one of the main obstacles to their development and, above all, to their survival. so does the world need an extra dose of free trade or a new approach to development? can the eradication of poverty in the acp countries be achieved by 'all-purpose trade'? should it not be primarily in the service of development, of meeting the needs of the people? is it not therefore a question first of tackling the structural causes which are generating impoverishment? in our view, these problems are essentially due to the inadequacy of production and marketing structures, which are geared to the immediate export of raw materials instead of promoting processing on the spot and south-south trade. non-tariff barriers are also the main obstacles to access to the eu market. as for the systems designed to ensure guaranteed prices, have they not lacked the means to prevent the efforts of the developing countries from being ruined by adverse economic conditions? finally, the introduction of conditionality criteria for structural consisted in offering advantages which are themselves obstacles to be overcome. one african expert sums it up this way: we can export computers, sports cars and nuclear plant equipment duty-free, the downside is that we don't manufacture them. it is a thrilling news that we can export sorghum, cassava, unfortunately, the european consumer does not want it. in these circumstances, is the urgency to establish new free trade agreements, or rather to invest in production tools and to relax the conditions for granting manufacturing patents? this is the whole point of the negotiations in parallel with the wto. the european union and the acp countries together constitute a considerable proportion of the wto members, a majority, a force which can and must influence the negotiations until 2005, by recognising the rights of developing countries. these suffer from structural economic weaknesses which warrant special treatment to address the causes of global inequalities. is it not urgent to devise a special and differentiated approach which can respond to the new challenges and which includes both long-term commercial, financial and technological measures aimed at building sustainable capacities in each of the areas where there is inequality between countries? let me finish by addressing a few specific questions. what is the likely impact of free trade areas on the social, economic - mr president, the report rightly argues that the results of the so-called acp-eu partnership are the opposite of its claim to promote and accelerate economic development. instead of seeing an increase in their exports to the european union, the acp countries have seen their exports to the eu almost halve since the signing of the agreement. instead of improving, the terms of trade between the european union and the acp countries have deteriorated. instead of developing, these countries have become poorer. the only conclusion to be drawn is that the objectives set out in the lomé convention, the cotonou agreement, etc., have nothing to do with reality. behind the appearance of a system of preferences, these agreements promote the plundering of the poor countries by the big capital of the rich countries of europe. in the colonial past, this plunder was done openly and shamelessly. today, when the former colonies have become independent, we do not speak of dictates but of negotiations, not of exploitation but of partnership, but the system remains the same. trade relations between imperialist and poor countries are established in such a way that the former continue to enrich themselves while the latter continue to be impoverished. we share the rapporteur's opposition to the commission's proposal to set up free trade areas. the freedom that is being talked about is like letting the wolf into the sheepfold. but it would be futile to try to improve a system that is fundamentally flawed. the only way for poor countries to be saved is for the world economic system to be radically transformed.

in writing. - mrs hautala's report on the quality of petrol and diesel shows serious economic competence for farms and forests. first, it extends to non-road mobile machinery (agricultural and forestry tractors in particular) the fuel quality standards which are applicable to all road vehicles. this is in our view covered by the emnr (non-road mobile engines) directive. secondly, the lower sulphur levels for non-road mobile machinery will lead to an increase of 8 to 10% in the price per litre. this measure will increase the quality of diesel on the market, with the result that there will be significant logistical problems, without any real environmental added value. finally, the obligation to use a new class of fuel in agriculture will require the replacement of storage tanks, at an average cost of eur 5 000 per farm. for a sector such as agriculture, already weakened by the health crises and awaiting the new guidelines of the cap, this is a significant additional cost. in order not to risk ruining this sector, we prefer to exclude the emnr and to stick to the realism of the council's common position.
in writing. - we want to distance ourselves from the hautala report. the aim of reducing the sulphur content of petrol and diesel is certainly commendable, but the significant logistical problems posed by the proposal do not seem to bring about any proven environmental improvement. when the report was considered by the committee on the environment, neither the rapporteur nor the commission itself was able to give an opinion on the various cost-benefit aspects of such an initiative. we are against the inclusion of fuels for non-road vehicles in the directive from 2005 onwards. this is an unrealistic proposal and risks further weakening agricultural enterprises. it would be appropriate to review the issue of full alignment of vehicles at the 2005 interim date. we also oppose the dismantling of existing derogations concerning the sulphur content of petrol and diesel, in order to continue to meet the constraints of supplying the outermost regions. finally, we regret that the need to change the volatility limit for ethanol and petrol mixtures has not been recognised. this measure is intended to enable member states to include ethanol-added petrol in order to meet the targets set by the proposal for a biofuels directive. in writing. - we approved the resolution on the outcome of the johannesburg world summit on sustainable development, because it shows, and this is very positive, that european countries have a broadly shared perception of these issues, and that they show a high level of sensitivity. on this basis, the european union and its member states can act and hopefully become the leading players in the world environment sector in the future. although the actual results of johannesburg are not up to the task (because one can only be appalled by the scale of global environmental problems), the union has been able to play a stimulating role, for example in the launching of partnerships on water, sanitation and energy. among the particular reservations i would like to highlight three: the main one concerns the over-emphasis on the role that the union has allowed the wto to play in arbitrating between trade and environmental rules; secondly, the gradual dismantling of agricultural export subsidies is a desirable objective, but certainly not that of all internal aid; and finally, parliamentarians have not been sufficiently involved in the preparatory coordination work.

in writing. - in 1992 the earth summit was held in rio de janeiro, and the question of sustainable development was raised. since then, many conferences have been held. the johannesburg conference should have been an opportunity to put into practice all the good intentions expressed over the last 10 years in a courageous and voluntary plan of action. today i am disappointed with the poor results. there is no need to list again the shortcomings of the adopted action plan. i simply wish to emphasize the insufficient place given to research policy in the debate on sustainable development. while the primary role of science is to measure the state of the environment and report back to policy makers and the public, it is expected to formulate solutions to environmental problems. europe, which has established its european research area, an area open to the world, must be able to share its scientific knowledge and experience with developing countries. the latter are faced with a difficult equation to solve, namely the need to assume strong and rapid growth with all the damage that this can cause in social and environmental terms!
in writing. - far from drawing the lessons from the ecological and social crisis ravaging the planet, the johannesburg summit has given the measure of the irresponsibility of states. the bush administration bears a great deal of responsibility for the freezing of the negotiations. but the european union showed no more arrogance by sticking to the unacceptable decisions of doha and monterrey. if the eu really wanted to help the development of the south, it would remove agricultural export subsidies which put products on the market at competitive prices. the common agricultural policy still operates on a productivist logic that multiplies surpluses. there is an urgent need to refocus direct aids to promote sustainable agriculture. against the wto's call for a general opening of borders, poor countries must be able to protect their agriculture by introducing tariff protections to stabilise domestic prices. the financing needs for access to clean water, energy, health and transport are enormous. we must put an end to the imf's strangulation of public budgets by structural adjustment policies and cancel the external debt of the countries of the south. states must regain their sovereignty in defining their development priorities. the resolution before parliament does not take sufficient account of these issues, which is why i abstain.
in writing. - the concept of sustainable development is based on a need: to respond to the sense of complexity and dependence that characterizes globalisation by solidarity with a concern for the future. but what project of global community do we propose for future generations? 'terminological antidotes' are being brandished as a panacea; the concept of sustainable development is one of them. in an environment discourse where the precautionary principle has become a policy and good governance a myth, this notion has a good chance of feeding on itself and justifying itself. this principle, which is vague and calls for transparency in decisions, is sometimes very opaque. today's resolution is the very type of text which has been submitted to us on this subject. the commission's proposal is based on a number of statements of intent which can only be unanimously agreed, and opens the door to technical, sometimes questionable, elements. today it is a reform of the cap and the community's trade policy and, by extension, of the fisheries policy. it is not a question of denigrating a strong and mobilizing concept, but of marking its vigilance in the face of the risk of its exploitation. we therefore propose to return to the interpretation of the brundtland report, which defined sustainable development in terms of the direction to be given to action. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this field, including the establishment of a european centre for the development of vocational training (ecvet) and the establishment of a european centre for vocational training (ecvet).
in writing. - it is rather unpleasant, when reading the european parliament's resolution on the international criminal court (icc), to discover in every line a certain arrogance on the part of the union, which wants to force the hand of states, member states, candidates or third parties, to adhere to the statutes of the court, or refuse to sign bilateral agreements with non-members. as if the european union alone had access to higher universal principles which told it that the court must have universal jurisdiction. but it is not so. the icc is based on a treaty which only binds its parties. therefore, the united states is entitled to make it clear that, if it does not sign, its nationals cannot be referred to the court without their consent. by claiming or implying otherwise, the union is wrong and unnecessarily complicates transatlantic relations. in fact, when you see this european arrogance, you think the united states is right to be wary. how far would she go? it is good to remind him, however, that it could be dangerous to abandon the traditional rules of international order in favor of a world justice that, without the consent of the nations, would be based on nothing.
in writing. - as regards the scandalous nature of the remarks made against the united states, i will simply observe that, by condemning their refusal - which is perfectly legal and legitimate - to accede to the rome statute of the international criminal court, adopted in 1998, parliament is committing a major act of interference in the internal affairs of a sovereign state. and in the name of what ? from a so-called international criminal law imposing itself, god only knows why and how, on the members of the "international community". clearly, the moralists of cosmopolitan "well-thinking" have learned nothing. the icc will be to human rights what the sdn was to peacekeeping: an empty shell ! the effectiveness of a legal order depends not only on its normative production but also on its ability to impose its law through its 'monopoly of legitimate violence'. public order requires a public power, an empire that can exercise coercion. the judge is nothing without the power of the sword. if the icc is to be anything more than a gadget, then an international public power must be instituted, and therefore a world government! we reject this imperialist logic, which may claim to be universalist humanism.
in writing. - the joint resolution, which brings together the right and left of parliament in a touching unanimity, and which refers to the relations between the european union and mercosur, this common market involving four latin american countries, including brazil and argentina, intends, among other things, to 'reexamine and solve the problem of the external debt of the four countries' at a time when argentina's bankruptcy is spreading to uruguay and now threatens brazil. the european union is invited to provide financial support to mercosur. even amended by vague promises of aid for the various "solidarity economy initiatives" that the population had to take to survive, the resolution above all argues that mercosur remains a boon for european companies whose exports had tripled in five years and who are the main partners of mercosur. european companies would like to maintain their small presence in the backyard of the united states. but it is precisely the application of this predatory policy, which is increasingly favouring the capitalist groups, both american and european, and from which the possessing classes of latin america have profited, that has plunged the majority of the population into unemployment and misery. continuing with this policy of plunder could only worsen his misery. that is why we voted against this resolution.
in writing. - the joint resolution recalls that 'the eu is the main trading partner and the largest direct investor in the mercosur countries'. we still have to look back on these investments. these are directly linked to the liberal policies of structural adjustment. for example, french companies such as edf, suez lyonnaise and france telecom have taken advantage of the wave of privatisation of public services to enter these 'markets' with the sole aim of making profits. this has resulted in redundancies for workers and increases in fares for users. the best part is that a company like edenor in argentina, the main subsidiary of edf, is today asking the government to renegotiate its debt and an agreement to increase its tariffs! privatizing profits and socializing losses, that is what the resolution calls the "strategic and solidarity-based commitment of the union to the mercosur countries with their economic and political integration projects"! mass layoffs, precariousness, unemployment, poverty, the dismantling of public services - this is the policy of the imf that the mercosur countries have applied. we, for our part, reaffirm our full solidarity with the popular movements developing in these countries, and particularly in argentina. the first minimum step that europe could take would be the total cancellation of the debt of the mercosur countries. as none of this is in the resolution, i voted against it.
in writing. - when it deals with the institutional organization of the common foreign and security policy (cfsp), the brok report remains in line with the model of the traditional european parliament positions: it draws the cfsp as far as it can in the direction of communitization, calling in particular for 'common diplomacy, if not a single one' (paragraph 12), qualified majority voting in the council (paragraph 14), the transfer of the post of high representative for the cfsp from the council to the commission (paragraph 11). these proposals are the result of an abstract projection at european level of the conception of a federal state, and not of a reflected apprehension of concrete realities. the common foreign and security policy cannot draw its strength from artificial community procedures. it will only be achieved if the nations join. in these circumstances, it must be based on these, which implies: the maintenance of the coordinating function in the council; decision by unanimity, or, failing that, variable geometry; the location of the instruments with the council, and not the commission. the convention, under the presidency of valéry giscard d'estaing, must remain lucid and resist the federalist bombardment if it is to be effective.
in writing. - this report on progress in implementing the cfsp comes at a time when everyone is aware of the abysmal absence of europe on the international scene! what a paradox ! yet europe still has the same stubborn will to ignore the reality that today one state is sovereignly using its colossal power to impose its hegemony. the attitude of the united states towards, for example, iraq is regrettable. but it is also the expression of a geopolitical constant according to which international relations are primarily determined by states whose behaviour is the result of a free assessment of their vital interests. the problem for europe is that it is faced with a nation which, already immensely powerful, is also benefiting from the disappearance of the great european diplomacies. european integration, far from being an added value, is a bottom-up approach to diplomacy that maintains the imbalance of powers. the community of a virtual cfsp would therefore be a serious historical contradiction: it would further restrict the member states, whereas the freedom of our nations is, in the field of foreign policy as elsewhere, the condition for the independence of europe; this does not exclude cooperation between states or the freely discussed and agreed coordination of their policies.
in writing. - we obviously voted against this report which has the stupid pretence of moralizing the arms trade. we are against the trafficking of arms, whether it is official, unofficial or illegal. it is not easy to distinguish between these three categories of trafficking, when we know how many cases of arms trafficking involve ministers, whether they are still in office or not, or so-called officials! it would be better to devote the productive capacity of the community to something other than weapons. and it is criminal to further the debt of poor countries, who are already out of breath, by selling, even legally, weapons to their leaders, which they will use against their own people.

the council. - madam president, may i emphasize that the signing of the association agreement has really marked a turning point and opened a new chapter in our relations with algeria. the council considers that the signing of this agreement clearly demonstrates the willingness of the algerian authorities to continue and intensify their efforts in the reform process needed to stimulate trade and investment. this should also be reflected in political and social reforms. it also sends a clear signal to investors that algeria is committed to creating a constructive environment for international businesses. the agreement is primarily about intergovernmental relations, but it also provides a framework for business and civil society. the agreement also has implications for the union's entire mediterranean policy and represents a further step towards the creation of a euro-mediterranean free trade area. the agreement also aims to promote subregional cooperation between the mediterranean partners themselves, which is so important for a positive outcome of the barcelona process. the association agreement contains an article on the mobility of persons and the eu has therefore committed itself to exploring the possibility of simplifying and speeding up the procedures for issuing visas to certain persons. this provision shall be incorporated into the rules for the implementation of the agreement. once the agreement enters into force, the bodies set up by it will have to examine how this commitment on visas could be implemented - taking account of the union's policy at that time, of course. as regards respect for human rights, the council is following very closely the issues relating to respect for human rights in algeria, particularly in the context of the political dialogue with algeria which has been taking place at ministerial level since 1997. this gives the council, represented by the troika, the opportunity to address these issues regularly and to emphasize strongly that any violations and any abuses must be avoided, including in the fight against terrorism. the association agreement will now provide greater opportunities for monitoring this issue and for supporting the algerian authorities in this regard. i would point out that, as is well known, the agreement makes respect for human rights an essential element underpinning the external and internal policies of the parties. it also provides an institutional framework for regular political dialogue at various levels, in particular within the association council, on all issues of common interest. as long as respect for human rights is a problem in algeria, the question will be on the agenda of the joint meetings. this applies both to the political dialogue established in 1997 and to the bodies of the agreement, in particular the association council and the association committee, once the agreement enters into force. the council does not intend to make any enquiries on the situation in kabylie, as it considers the matter to be an internal algerian matter in the first instance. the council nevertheless welcomes the important decision recently taken to grant the tamazight language the status of national language. in general, the european council in gothenburg in june 2001 urged all those responsible in algeria to take action to put an end to the current confrontations and violence. it called on the authorities to launch a political initiative to resolve the crisis through dialogue between all algerians. however, the situation remains difficult and complex, as evidenced by the low turnout in the parliamentary elections on 30 may 2002. the local elections in october can also provide an important indication of the situation in the region. a solution can be helped along by improving the socioeconomic situation, and we are fully prepared to help in the effort of economic reform. we are supporting them through the meda regulation, which is eur 240 million for the period 2000-04, and the european investment bank loans of eur 620 million since 1996. the new investment facility should also help to support the economic situation in algeria once it is in place. the association agreement provides for the association council to facilitate cooperation and contacts between the european parliament and the parliamentary institutions of algeria, as well as between the economic and social committee and the corresponding body in algeria. i would like to stress that the council welcomes the conclusions of the latest meeting of the euro-mediterranean parliamentary forum in bari in june 2002. the parliamentary dimension of our partnership with the southern mediterranean countries was emphasized. we are in the process of examining the cooperation mechanisms that can be used to create such a euro-mediterranean assembly.
the commission. madam president, the agreement signed between the european union and algeria marks a new era in our relations and i would agree with mr brok that algeria needs europe and europe needs algeria in the context of euro-mediterranean cooperation. i would like to mention three important points, which i believe also answer the questions raised by mr brok. the first is the economic and political reforms that can be fostered by this agreement, the second is the free movement of persons and the third is human rights. the first point is that, politically, algeria chose in 1989 to adopt a constitution which provides for multiparty democracy. today democracy is not working in depth, political life is cut off from civil society. it is up to algeria to improve the situation and, above all, to ensure a genuine separation of executive, legislative and judicial powers and the transparency of electoral processes. the political dialogue provided for in the association agreement provides a valuable framework for exchanging views and experience on this issue. the association agreement provides for the gradual establishment of a single free trade area between algeria and the european union. this is a challenge for the algerian government to make the necessary reforms. as the resolution stresses, certain basic needs of the population related to water, housing, health care must first be met, otherwise it is obvious that the government will not be able to achieve any other reforms because it will not have the popular consensus. it also needs to make the transition, to facilitate the transition from the current state-controlled economic model to a market economy. this reform was necessary in any case in algeria, where the suffocating state model has reached its limits. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the transition to a free economy will require consultation with business associations, with trade unions, and should focus on improving a legal framework for business and investment, reforming the banking system and cracking down on corruption. the government has recently approved a $7 billion programme to this end, covering many of these issues. the aid provided by the european union through the meda programme is also complementary to the meda programme, since it has three main objectives. the first is to strengthen the market economy, the second is to develop human resources and the third is to consolidate the rule of law to meet certain needs. the second issue concerns the free movement of persons. the agreement gives the european union the task of finding ways of simplifying the visa procedure, as mr frederiksen said, especially for those involved in its application. this is a reasonable request from the algerian side. the association agreement cannot only concern the establishment of a free trade area, but should also facilitate the two-way movement of persons. it should be said that this project concerns legal movements and in no way contradicts the conclusions of seville concerning the suspension of illegal immigration. the agreement signed is fully in line with the seville guidelines, which provide for specific cooperation in the field of illegal immigration and the readmission of illegal immigrants. the third point is the human rights clause. it is an essential part of the association process. the commission is well aware that algeria has experienced a tragic experience of terrorist acts in the last decade and we are providing all possible support to the algerian government in the fight against terrorism, but we also believe that no violation of fundamental freedoms can be accepted in the context of this fight against terrorism. association under the barcelona process implies a common commitment to respect certain basic democratic norms and values. the main concern in this area is the missing and there are very significant obstacles which must be overcome both by the families of the missing and by the non-governmental organisations, which often encounter distracting procedures from the authorities. i believe that the application of the human rights clause can be dealt with both procedurally and substantially. the european union must be able to take action, through the political dialogue, which must be structured around human rights and, in substance, i would say, the european union, using clearer and more substantive language, with fewer evasions. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area, including the establishment of a european centre for the development of vocational training. we hope that a dialogue with representative bodies can be resumed and we welcome the conciliatory approach recently initiated on the issue of official recognition of tamazight as a national language. the european parliament is willing, as has already been said, to develop a dialogue with the algerian parliament, which is extremely important for mutual information, for common positions, for the interests of both sides. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. in general, the commission warmly supports the approval by parliament of this association agreement, which should not be seen as a blank check on the algerian government, but as an encouragement to carry out the political, economic and social reforms it is promoting, especially for the betterment of the algerian people.

- madam president, since the coup d'état of 19 september, côte d'ivoire has been in a confused military situation throughout the north of its territory. military operations are continuing as we speak and fighting rages in bouaké, raising fears of the worst for the civilian population caught in the crossfire. my dear colleagues, we are trembling for the ivorian people who are being held hostage by the factions and who are paying for this crisis with their freedom and sometimes with their lives. we are worried that côte d'ivoire may be moving a little further away from this model which has been so often praised. today, the country is torn apart, ivorian society is in flames and blood and we tremble for africa and africans. the whole region is in danger of being shaken, a region which has already seen too many wars, too many human tragedies, and where the roaming of armed gangs and trafficking of all kinds are a painful reality. this solution does not seem to be entirely unrelated to the current destabilization of côte d'ivoire. to destabilise côte d'ivoire is to lay the foundations for a crisis comparable to those of the great lakes or the congo which have torn the centre of the continent apart for many years. so this crisis is worrying us, and it's saddening us. but it also surprises us. it comes at a time when the efforts of the laurent gbagbo regime were bearing fruit on two major issues in the country. firstly, national reconciliation, with the organisation of a broad forum in 2001, and the formation of a government of national unity bringing together the main political forces after the elections in july 2002. then economic and social recovery, with fundamental social reforms like free schooling and universal health care. but to continue along this path, côte d'ivoire needs peace. europe must press for a negotiated solution and a peaceful solution to the crisis. it should support all mediation efforts and welcome the actions undertaken under the aegis safeguarding of the unity of the entire territory of côte d'ivoire in accordance with constitutional legality. we must be careful that the possible dispatch of an intervention force does not lay the foundations for a de facto partition of the country. the socialist group also supports the sending of a parliamentary mission - i say this to my colleagues in parliament - to express our support for the democratically elected institutions and to meet the various ivorian political forces. however, in order to continue to consolidate democracy in côte d'ivoire, president gbagbo will have to take ouatara from the presidential candidacy. it does not provide for the possibility of dissolving the national assembly in the event of a major crisis and this may open the way to a political reaction of the most violent. finally, president gbagbo will have to resume dialogue to pursue without reservation and without ambiguity the effort of national reconciliation indispensable to a country torn apart for years by the manipulation of the concept of ivory and which has almost 30% of foreigners. in this connection, the call for the expulsion of 500,000 burkinabé people made last sunday by ivorian - madam president, the recent events in côte d'ivoire, marked by numerous murders, are very worrying. the military uprising against the current legal government is unjustifiable no matter how bad the economic and political conditions are. the unprecedented economic crisis linked to the fall in the prices of raw materials, especially coffee and cotton, has widened poverty and misery in the country. but it is also clear that the trivialization of the concept of ivory, which culminated in the 2000 presidential elections, has only fuelled the climate of hatred and violence in the country, and accusations against neighboring countries of supporting the mutineers could be used to justify the persecution of the immigrant civilian population. in this respect, we should welcome the speech by president gbagbo calling for the protection of foreigners. still, it would be necessary for him to be heard by his troops. the risk of a xenophobic civil explosion is great. we must avoid the possibility of an interethnic civil war, a congolese-style crisis scenario, which would be extremely dangerous and regrettable for côte d'ivoire and all its inhabitants. as such, while it is regrettable that ecowas mediation failed to bring about the resumption of negotiations between the government and the rebels, it should not be the case that interventionist forces actually mark an ethnic partition on the ground. the european union must support the legitimate government in order to re-establish the rule of law and protect the civilian population, regardless of ethnicity. in the longer term, a commission of inquiry should be set up to shed light on the events and to convict those responsible. the european union must ensure respect for the principles of human rights, democracy and political pluralism, but also, and this is essential, promote the economic and social development of côte d'ivoire.
- madam president, ladies and gentlemen, representatives of the member states, commissioners, let me express my astonishment at the arguments of some of my colleagues, because, after all, the situation in côte d'ivoire is so clear that it should spontaneously bring us to an agreement on some obvious points. the first obvious thing is that côte d'ivoire is one of the countries which should receive our most active support, because there are many encouraging signs: a growth rate of 3%, a relatively rapid march towards democracy, marked by presidential elections which are hailed everywhere as progress, a process of formation of political forces which, after the forum for national reconciliation, was to lead to fully democratic parliamentary elections, and the present government must be given the task of organising them as soon as possible. yes, côte d'ivoire and its president gbagbo deserve the support of all european states concerned about relations with africa. i do not understand why anyone should hesitate, unless he is willing to accept the policy of the worst or to indulge in an indifference which, i fear, is tempting to many europeans, but which a frenchman cannot accept. secondly, there is no civil war in côte d'ivoire. it is simply dealing with foreign aggression which, while it uses old ethnic antagonisms, as usual, comes first in geopolitical analysis. the so-called insurgents are obviously armed, and heavily armed, by one or more foreign powers. the analysis of the situation is therefore not based on ethnographic considerations, much less humanitarian complaints, but on geopolitical analysis. and here is the third, most important, but perhaps for this reason too often overlooked, fact, that the ignorance - or blindness - of our assembly in geopolitical matters is common to so many subjects. africa is today, of all the continents, the one that escapes the influence of the world empire the most. this is for historical reasons linked to the ties that several european nations have forged with it and, correlatively, to the fear, which has often stopped washington, that any destabilization of the regimes would be the bed of the soviet union. but since the collapse of the russian power, the empire has tended to extend its influence over this continent which is both the richest, potentially the least, and sadly the most vulnerable of all. this has led to several attempts in equatorial africa, formerly belgium, which have extended to the countries bordering the oil-rich gulf of guinea. the ambitions of a man of uncertain nationality, who in any case spent most of his life in the united states, are now being exploited to destabilise a country whose position was consolidating year by year and which was consequently becoming a major partner of europe. it's that attachment point, that bond that we want to destroy. my dear colleagues, let us be firm on the real interests of europe. france has the courage to do so. the support it gives to the legal and democratic government of côte d'ivoire must be shared by all europeans. because what france does in africa, it does not do for itself alone, it does for the whole of europe.

- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i am entering this debate on the establishment of a european union solidarity fund with a feeling of regret and satisfaction. i regret that we were not heard in the aftermath of the catastrophic storms of december 1999, the stigmas of which are still very much alive in many parts of france and europe. the european union must finally admit that it must be present at the same time as the distress and tragedies affecting our fellow citizens in their lives and in their property. i would like to congratulate commissioner barnier and his services, and our colleague mr rolf berend, in particular, on their exceptional responsiveness to this matter. i believe that this report is a credit to both the commission and parliament, and to the european union as a whole, both for its speed and its balance, its recognition of the exceptional nature of disasters, and its emphasis on urgency, flexibility and adaptability. it is true that disasters can be dramatic or felt to be so, regardless of their size, and it seems to me that tonight, as we finally put in place a system capable of intervening in major events, we must also think about our presence in the face of distress, tragedies or natural disasters of a more modest dimension. there are no significant deaths or minor deaths. there are, unfortunately, no major ruins or ruins that would be indifferent to us. that is why i would like to take this opportunity once again, and thank commissioner barnier for mentioning it, to call for the creation of a european civil security corps, not ex nihilo, but to enable civilian rescuers in the colours of the union to be deployed and projected to the regions in difficulty, thus demonstrating our solidarity in distress.
- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i too would like to express my satisfaction at the rapid creation of this emergency aid fund, which can be mobilised in the event of major mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the approach which has led to the proposal for a regulation which we are debating this evening is exemplary and deserves to be given serious consideration at a time when we are going to have to update the common fisheries policy. it was about 15 years ago that french fishermen from boulogne-sur-mer began exploiting and marketing certain species of fish living beyond the continental shelf in the abyssal pit, more than half a mile deep. at the request of these fishermen, a scientific institute, the ifremer, has begun to take a close interest in the biology of these species, in particular their life cycle. a good collaboration between professionals and scientists has made it possible to determine quite early that these species have slow life cycles and that there was an urgent need to limit the sampling in order not to endanger their biological balances. at the request of the fishermen, supported by scientists, the government of the first member state concerned, france, asked the commission to intervene to regulate these new fisheries by establishing tacs and quotas. the commission has been reluctant and slow to react for a long time. without a political agreement at the fisheries council last june, it is not certain that we would have these two proposals for regulations on deep-sea fisheries today. but here they are, and i welcome them, and the report of our colleague michael holmes, who has dealt with this matter with great competence and to whom i wish a speedy recovery. the genesis of these regulations is exemplary in more than one respect. first of all, it illustrates the fact that fishermen are the first to be affected and the first to be involved in setting the rules for sustainable fishing. it then shows that the instruments best suited to ensuring effective protection of fisheries species are flexible and reversible instruments, such as tacs and quotas, rather than rigid structural measures with irreversible effects, such as ship-wrecking and the conversion of fishermen. it also shows that fishermen and scientists can work closely and intelligently together and come up with proposals for realistic and constructive management measures that allow for activity while conserving the resource. it shows that a top-down approach, from the ground up to the competent authority, is more effective than a bottom-up or even condescending approach, as the commission unfortunately does most often, and especially when it launches the cfp reform project. these lessons must therefore be carefully preserved and applied, if possible, to the whole of the current reform process. i think that the commission has a duty to ensure that the fishermen are not forced to pay for the damage they have caused to the fisheries sector.
- mr president, the proposal for a directive to establish a system for the exchange of greenhouse gas emission allowances is an early application and a gradual learning within the community of the definitive system which will have to come into force after 2008, under the terms of the kyoto protocol. the kyoto principle is simple. the aim is to make the emitters of greenhouse gases pay the price for the invisible and unquantified damage they cause to the environment, and thus to the whole community. since this infringement of a collective good is not automatically included in the prices, the idea is to create a market for pollution rights whose securities will be defined, quantified and sold by the public authorities. of course, they will be reduced gradually, and then pollution will be reduced. first of all, this system is ingenious. it combines the role of public authority with market procedures and we should wish it well. secondly, we should also congratulate the european community and its members for actively supporting it and for voluntarily setting up, from 2005 to 2007, an experimental formula which will enable us to get the system running, to position ourselves better to meet our emission reduction commitments after 2008 and, hopefully, to play a pioneering role vis-à-vis other continents. the learning formula is based on the free allocation of emission allowances to five thousand large companies in sensitive sectors. these allowances will be tradable at community level, allowing operators who have achieved emission savings to take advantage of their residual allowances by selling them on an over-the-counter basis to those who need them. we can support these provisions, but we must also stress that the free allocation of allowances may not continue beyond 2008, because beyond learning, the objective must be to make the hidden costs of these emissions pay for themselves in full, and not just marginally at the time of transfer. as regards our reservations, we would stress that the proposed system applies initially to carbon dioxide alone, but that it is desirable, in order to avoid distortions, to consider now how to extend it without too much delay to all greenhouse gases. in addition, the initial allocation of emission allowances, which will first be based on national plans, will have to be harmonised from 2008 onwards, following a comitology procedure whose ins and outs and criteria are poorly understood, and all this seems to us to be far too vague and should be clarified. nevertheless, in general terms, we think the system is good and we will support the moreira da silva report.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, what a new member like myself finds when she comes to the european parliament, to the committee on culture, is that there is no coherent vision of culture in europe. and i prefer to use the term "vision" rather than cultural "politics". who says cultural politics, says debate, dispute, that we could have. but when we say that there is no coherent vision, it simply means that, for example, film is treated from the point of view of the industry, that music can be supported in the budget lines, but that this is limited, and that we do not see how the language or languages inherent in the practice of theatre can be taken into account. that is why i wanted to draw up this own-initiative report, mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen. this report was a way for me to bridge, in this vast cultural area of europe, the gap between industry and music, which is working so well. when we look at languages, theatre and live entertainment, what we also find is that, at the heart of it, it is our heritage. this theatre, this living spectacle, is europe's heritage, both literary and political, since there is no theatre that has not been defined both by the birth of democracy and by the life of the agora and the city. that is why i believe that the question of the theatre and the live spectacle is becoming very important in the european area. when i first started meeting with the entertainment industry, the first thing that came to my mind was their demand for freedom. there was no question of them losing their freedom, of being taken by the hand, of being made an official art form that would not be at all in keeping with what they were looking for. that was the first thing they said. the second thing they mentioned was all their difficulties, their innumerable difficulties, including double taxation, social and fiscal, but also the innumerable difficulties they have to move around. because they move, the artists: they are already in this europe, they do not ask themselves whether they are staying at home or becoming uprooted beings, they move and they need help to move. it's a kind of reality that exists and we have to follow it. of course, i do not think that we can apply the rules of the market and competition to the cultural space, and we learn this every day. we have seen it elsewhere; in the cinema sector, state aid is now recognised, even promoted or modelled in countries other than those where it already exists. and so, even for this audiovisual industry, we know the importance of the supporting role of the state. i believe that for live entertainment and theatre in particular, it is the same thing, there must be state aid and this aid begins with the responsibility that the states must take to facilitate the movement of people and productions in europe, as well as to promote training. in a way, that is simply the conclusion of my report. the states must take their share of the responsibility for cooperation. and eventually, we might stop thinking in terms of cleavage. i think that in the debate we have on culture, there is always the same argument: either it will be community or it will be subsidiarity, and therefore it must not be touched. i don't think this division is going to do any good, that it's not going to help us at all. on the contrary, if we take up article 151 with its request for cultural cooperation, we are exactly where we need to be if we are to think about a europe of culture and a europe of the spectacle. as i said, there are obstacles: double taxation, the absence of legal standards, a common technical vocabulary. but there are also remedies, the overheading, the white paper which could help us to harmonize legislation - and i hope the commission will be kind to us - the databases, the pooling of all the vocabulary. perhaps we should also take the advice of experts, artists, so that they are informed when it comes to making decisions. in conclusion, ladies and gentlemen, i think we must think about how culture will be preserved and properly dealt with in the convention and in the future constitution. i would also like to mention the european council resolution which proposed a plan for cooperation in the field of culture in june. i hope that we, together with the european commission and parliament, will also be able to follow the resolutions of the european council.

commission. – mr president, before briefly introducing the three commission proposals, i would like to thank and congratulate the two rapporteurs, mrs müller and mrs grossetête, as well as the committee on the environment, public health and consumer policy for all the work and effort they have put into finalising these three reports. let me start with the objectives of the proposals. there are three. first and foremost, to guarantee a high level of health protection for european citizens, and that is always the starting point. secondly, to increase the availability of innovative medicinal products and, at the same time, favour competition with generic products, and, thirdly, to prepare for enlargement, which will very soon become a reality. as far as the concrete proposals are concerned, i will concentrate on three of them. first, the need to reinforce the role of the european medicines evaluation agency and the centralised procedure. why? because the objective is to make new innovative medicines available to all eu citizens, at the same time. this is a question of equality of all patients in europe. thus, the commission has proposed that the centralised authorisation procedure for all medicines containing new active substances be made mandatory. this is the community solution to the issue of innovation availability and i hope that this house will support it. additionally, this would produce economies of scale, save resources and time and, finally, lead to improved regulatory efficiency. the commission wants, especially in the enlarged eu, to ensure that patients have quicker access to innovative medicines. the mutual recognition procedure has shown its limits. the evaluation process at the london agency takes an average of 180 days – clearly fewer than the maximum of 210 days provided for in the legislation. the centralised procedure would also be positive for small and medium-sized enterprises. let us take the example of biotechnology. smes are very active in this field, where centralised authorisation is already mandatory. experience has not brought any major problems to light. the benefits of a centralised procedure for smes are obvious in areas such as orphan drugs, where most of the marketing authorisations are granted to smes. this said, the commission could, with a view to an overall solution, seek supporting measures for smes if there are particular obstacles, to help smes overcome them. secondly, we need to find the right balance between innovation and competition from generics. why is this so important? to put it in a nutshell, we need innovative products for the benefit of patients and we need generics to help reduce the pressure on health care costs. how then are these needs to be balanced? for innovative medicines, the commission proposes a new data-protection period. for generics, entry to the market will be speeded up. how will this happen? first, the commission proposes to harmonise the national data protection periods at 10 years across the board. this will provide a harmonised solution for europe. the protection period will give the innovative pharmaceutical industry an opportunity to recover its r& d investments. this will also allow for the smoother operation of the internal market. to reward further innovation and research in new products, the proposal provides for a possible extension of the protection period up to 11 years. for generics, the commission proposes to change a long-standing eu policy. we propose now, for the first time in eu legislation, that trials may begin on generics before the expiry of the patent or other form of intellectual property protection. this will speed up the marketing of generics on most of the national markets and will substantially help to increase competition. the commission believes that this is a balanced proposal. it takes account of the interests of the innovative european pharmaceutical industry, which is losing ground compared with the industry in the united states. it means fewer jobs and less research in europe unless we do things differently. at the same time, it will facilitate the development of a competitive market in generics, and that means medicines at lower cost for european citizens. finally, i should like to say a few words about controlled access to information for patients. i knew this would be a difficult discussion, but, first of all, the commission is not proposing an american type of direct advertising to patients. the discussions have concentrated to a large extent on the us model, but this is not our model. the facts of the matter are that a lot of fragmented information is already available on the web, at least for english-speaking patients. this has two major drawbacks: firstly, it discriminates against non-english-speaking people and, secondly, it means that the information can be piecemeal and unreliable. our proposal is that european citizens should obtain information that has been validated by european regulatory authorities and that follows guidelines to be agreed between the member states and the commission. it is a prudent proposal. it is a european pilot project, and has nothing in common with the us model. the alternatives to what we have today are, on the one hand, the continuation of massive direct advising to patients via the web. we cannot change this situation by our legislation. the alternative is to enable patients to obtain sound information, validated by the competent european authorities, on medicines for a small number of diseases. i think that this second option increases both choice and security for european patients. in conclusion, the commission proposals aim to guarantee a high level of public health to european citizens, to increase, in a balanced way, the availability of innovative medicinal products and generic products and also to be ready for enlargement. this is a challenging piece of legislation. i am looking forward to the debate in the house today and to continued cooperation with parliament and the council.
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, the subject we are discussing today is one of the most important of our legislature, since it concerns every european citizen. let me first of all thank all my colleagues from all the political groups for the discussions we have had and the work they have done through the 800 amendments. i think that there are a little too many amendments here, and rapid access to innovative and safe products, developing a preventive and continuous pharmacovigilance system and improving the competitiveness of the pharmaceutical sector in its search for new treatments. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area. a medicine is not a product like another. it is not bought and consumed like an ordinary everyday item. its use is unique, and everyone expects a medicine to be safe and effective. this safety, quality and efficacy are the three essential pillars of the european pharmaceutical industry. before a medicinal product is offered to the patient, it must go through specific and binding steps to obtain a marketing authorization. today we have two registration procedures: the centralised procedure, managed by the european agency, which issues a licence for all the countries of the union, and the mutual recognition procedure, which is the responsibility of the member states. we do not intend to change the existing dueling structure, but rather to optimise its operation. in fact, the question is about new active substances. we all agree that there is a difference between new active substances, which are about 20 per year, and new medicines, which are 200 to 300 per year. the commission therefore proposes to require the registration of these new molecules through a centralised procedure, in order to guarantee access to highly innovative therapies for all. some colleagues have expressed their wish to challenge this principle. i would like to say to them that we are faced with a crucial choice. because your choice will be a health choice or a market choice. the amendment which calls into question the scope of the directive will have to answer the following question: how can we explain to a patient that his european neighbour will have the opportunity to benefit from an innovative and effective treatment, but will have to wait a few years for authorization to be granted in his own country? in this context, let us take an extreme case in the context of enlargement: a slovenian and a portuguese person might have access to an innovative therapy, but a german or a cypriot would not have access to it. what are we doing, then, about the equality of the european citizen in health? some may say that the centralised procedure is costly for smes. but in the case of enlargement, 25 applications for marketing authorization through the decentralized procedure will cost even more. we all also bear in mind recent examples of medicines being withdrawn from the market for public health reasons. we know that the authorization of a medicinal product does not mean the end of the control of its efficacy and safety. the pharmacovigilance requirements should therefore be strengthened to provide the best possible guarantees for the patient, through random checks at the source of manufacture, through a publicly funded system which is a necessary guarantee of independence, and through a system for the rapid exchange of data collected by all partners, thus making it possible to ensure consistency of pharmacovigilance systems between member states. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this field, including the creation of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products (eamp), the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products (eamp) and the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products (eamp). the industry therefore needs to ensure the protection of this data. it is our duty to promote research to ensure the development of science, hence the interest in retaining our best researchers. it is also a question of ensuring patient safety, but also of preventing our european industries from being relegated to the second division in the global context, and left to the drawing board of the united states and asia. of course, the usefulness of generic drugs is no longer to be demonstrated. they play to the benefit of the sustainability of our european health systems. the introduction of appropriate measures, in particular through the bolar system, will therefore speed up their placing on the market. and let's remember that generics only grow through innovation. i also expect all member states to plan an information campaign for the general public to explain what a generic is, while emphasising its therapeutic equivalence with the reference medicine. with regard to veterinary medicines in particular, the major challenge is to deal with the problem of the availability of these medicines. a balance was sought between the relaxation of certain mechanisms such as the so-called "cascade" and the maintenance of the highest level of consumer safety in the case of food-producing animals. the cascade allows the use of medicines for other species, other diseases or even human medicines when no medicines are available for a particular disease or animal. this device has been enriched and extended for maximum efficiency and safety. the commission is proposing to extend the mandatory prescription to all medicinal products for food-producing animals, which is a problem for some member states, including ireland and the united kingdom. a compromise amendment, adopted by the committee on the environment, makes this measure consistent with national arrangements. finally, we cannot talk about the revision of european pharmaceutical legislation without touching on the subject of information and the commission's proposal, which aims to authorize on an experimental basis over five years, as well as the communication by the industry of information relating to certain medicines for the following conditions: asthma, aids, diabetes. the market for the medicinal product is unique and the objective pursued should not be to promote a maximum volume of sales. it is vital to maintain a very clear distinction between information and advertising and to strictly prohibit advertising. but it is no better information than that given by the doctor or pharmacist. however, information systems, particularly via the internet, have developed widely and it seems quite unfair that only people with access to the internet and who speak english should be able to collect this data and not others. it is our responsibility, however, to avoid any drift which leads to the development of incentive information, hidden, aimed at promoting the prescription, sale or consumption of a specific medicinal product. the environment committee overwhelmingly rejected the commission's proposal as being too ambiguous. but the problem is rejection. i wanted the notions of information and advertising to be better defined, and i proposed a system of validating information upstream by neutral scientific bodies. this proposal could form the basis for a new and thorough study which we expect from the commission. on the other hand, there is an indispensable source of information and information, i am talking about the notices. all the amendments tabled on this point are designed to improve their wording, clarity and comprehensibility. that's a very positive point. in conclusion, the importance of enlargement should be underlined. we cannot deny that the revision which will be adopted will apply to the new countries. that is why i have proposed what i shall call the 'generic euro'. in some candidate countries, for historical or economic reasons, reference medicines have never been registered. the updating of authorisations of generics to european legal requirements in the candidate countries therefore requires the possibility of referring to a reference product. the absence of such a product could lead to an obligation to withdraw from the market generic medicinal products which nevertheless comply with the requirements of quality, safety and efficacy. this situation creates problems of access to generic medicines. it therefore seems important that a reference medicinal product present in another member state can serve as a reference. each new candidate country has an important role to play as a full-fledged actor in the construction and development of the great europe of health that we all want. - mr president, we believe that the first objective of the revision of pharmaceutical legislation must be to ensure the safety, quality and efficacy of medicines placed on the european market, in order to protect public health. the committee on the environment has taken this into account by voting massively against any direct advertising for prescription medicines, while at the same time increasing the transparency of the marketing authorization procedures. patients have the right to objective and reliable information about their illnesses and the treatments available to treat them. but what better way to get this information than to make the database of all the medicines registered with the agency available to the public, together with the evaluation report on each drug, the reasons for its approval or rejection, and the explanatory note on the results of clinical trials, whether positive or negative? the initial evaluation, followed by a five-year management evaluation, provides an opportunity to consider the added therapeutic value of the medicinal products. this can only motivate european research and innovation. finally, we will oppose amendments which seek to limit the centralised procedure and give priority to the mutual recognition procedure, or to delay the marketing of generic medicines. we welcome the adoption in the committee on the environment of the amendments on the impact of medicines on the environment. my colleagues have followed us on this matter and we are quite satisfied. in conclusion, mr president, if the pharmaceutical companies have largely won the case in the commission's initial proposals, we must - and this must be the mission of the european parliament - protect the interests of citizens, patients and consumers.

be regarded as a regular operation. i would point out that parliament already has the means to encourage the commission to take further action. that is what has happened in recent years. the decision - mr president, discharge is a particularly important matter. this is one of the major powers of the european parliament and we saw this in the biggest crisis between parliament and the commission, which arose during the vote on discharge. i believe that the first objective pursued by this parliament over the last 15 years has been to ensure that the control exercised through discharge is political control in the best sense of the word, that is to say, control which is an expression of the will of the taxpayers to ensure the proper use of public money, and which is not limited to a mere technical formality. secondly, we felt that it was not just the commission but all the bodies with an autonomous budget which, by extension, should be given control of the discharge through the granting of the discharge by parliament. thirdly, we felt that since the treaty gave us the power to grant discharge, we should also have the power to refuse it. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. however, this extension of the landfill poses some problems. the first of these problems is the risk of prolonging a procedure indefinitely without result. the report presented to you by mr hans-peter martin provides for relatively short, relatively reasonable time limits for all the provisions. i would say to the commission: 'commissioner, you cannot ask for discharge in a short time and at the same time tell us that you are taking time to make the decisions necessary to bring yourself into line with the life of parliament. you have to choose: either you want extra time and they give you the discharge later, or you want a quick discharge and you do the diligence yourself". the second problem we have had is a technical problem of agreement between the three votes, namely the vote on discharge, the vote on the approval of the accounts and the vote on the resolution. that's three different votes for one decision, with the risk of inconsistency from one to the other. the report before you, which we strongly support in the epp group, solves the problem by combining the discharge procedure with the clearance of accounts procedure and by giving the president the opportunity to prevent a resolution from being put to the vote which would contradict the provisions on the vote on discharge by parliament. the third problem, which was the most serious and which we encountered repeatedly, was the problem of the majority. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we were at an impasse. the second risk was that we would have equal votes, either in committee or in parliament, whereas the treaty obliges us to take a decision. the report before you solves this problem in a way that is not entirely satisfactory, although in my opinion it is the best way possible. the report proposes to divide the procedure into two stages: in the first stage we would choose between granting and postponing, on the proposal of the cocobu; secondly, if the grant was not given at the end of the stay, we would have to choose between refusal and grant. and the option that would be rejected would then give rise to the adoption of the opposite option. this would avoid the deadlock we have constantly faced in the cocobu. this is a very good system and we very strongly support the compromise reached by the main groups. in this connection, i would like to thank the rapporteur in particular for his comments on the withdrawal of his request for a separate vote. a compromise is a whole, and we will stick to it, and we thank you for sticking to it. mr rapporteur, i wish you the best of luck.
