president of the republic of hungary. – mr president, first of all i would like to extend my sincere gratitude to the european parliament for commemorating the hungarian revolution of 1956. i stand here to address you for the first time at the plenary in hungarian. hopefully, it will very soon be one of the official languages of the european union. (applause) with your permission, however, i would anticipate this possibility now and will continue my address in hungarian. you will have the opportunity to listen to it in english, hopefully with a good interpretation the speaker continued in hungarian. what follows is the english interpretation.. i stand here deeply moved and overwhelmed when i recall with you the 1956 hungarian revolution, its martyrs and heroes. 23 october 1956 was an important moment in europe. we could even say what happened in hungary in 1956 was european history itself. both in budapest and all over the country, the people rose up and fought for freedom and democracy so that this country could once again be part of europe. the revolution grew into a freedom fight for the independence and sovereignty of hungary. the people had fought their revolution and freedom fight. thousands and thousands went to the barricades. the people were determined and they won. we were enriched in those days by wonderful examples of personal courage, heroism and self-sacrifice. on a single bloody morning, almost 100 people died in front of the parliament building in budapest. as a result of the uprising, the political regime collapsed and, in a few days, the forces of hungarian society established their own administration units in the form of workers' and national councils. the leaders of the revolution were aware that we hungarians could not defend our independence and regime on our own. the freedom fight came under attack by foreign troops on 4 november 1956 and was crushed a few days later, though resistance went on for quite a while. bloody retaliation followed. hundreds were executed, tens of thousands imprisoned. 23 october 1956 was perhaps the most european moment in our recent european and hungarian history. the european and hungarian spirit of freedom proved it would never surrender, it would never give in to the might of totalitarianism. (applause) great european thinkers, such as albert camus, françois mauriac and boris pasternak, to mention just a few, recognised the special importance of those events. albert camus wrote in november 1956: 'there is a genuine europe which is united in resisting tyranny in the name of truth and freedom. today, thousands of hungarian freedom fighters die for this europe'. françois mauriac saw the historical achievements of the revolution this way: 'when the stronger side is systematically inhuman, then perhaps the course of history is set by the will of the weaker'. camus and mauriac both understood then that the collapse of the revolution was probably unavoidable, that raw power would triumph again for a while. on the darkest day of reprisals and terror, 24 june 1958, when imre nagy, prime minister of the revolution, was executed, boris pasternak sent a postcard to budapest in french. disregarding soviet and hungarian censorship, as well as the personal risk he was taking, he wrote to his hungarian friend gyula illyés, author of a dramatic poem entitled 'a sentence on tyranny': 'whom can i possibly tell how saddened and shocked i am by the resurgence of inhuman atrocities, which we thought had gone for ever …'. as these witnesses of history put it, in this european moment the voices of truth and freedom were much weaker than those of tyranny and systematic cruelty. it showed the course of history, as mauriac said. these, and the moral courage and noble spirit which pasternak demonstrated even under the rule of tyranny, are the real spiritual values of europe. from the many personal stories told, we know that the 1956 revolution in hungary was a turning point in the lives of many leading european politicians. it influenced them in their choice of political career. that was when totalitarian dictatorship was finally unmasked. anyone who still had illusions about it realised its true meaning. during the era of retaliation after 1956, hundreds of thousands of hungarians fled to the west. a multitude of talented and honest hungarians showed the world what they were capable of when granted equal conditions, fair competition and solidarity, whether in europe or in america. they did much in order to keep up western awareness that the eastern part of europe must not be abandoned. while paying tribute to the memory of 1956, please allow me to express my thanks at this outstanding european forum to you for the helping hand extended to 200 000 hungarians. let us remember too those western europeans, who risked their lives in the hungarian revolution: journalists, ordinary people and one particular person who gave his life for the revolution, the noble and great danish diplomat bang-jensen. please forgive me for having spent so much time on one historical event, the 1956 hungarian revolution. i did so because this very spirit triumphed in central and eastern europe in 1989-1990. we know that this was a victory for the whole of europe, paving the way until the berlin wall fell, as mr cox said. the task is still the same: to remain faithful to this spirit. it is not easy. it is an enormous task which has to be broken down into small, troublesome, everyday tasks. let me quote camus again. in his essay 'the blood of hungarians' he said: 'it is hard for us to be worthy of so much sacrifice. yet we must try. let us forget our disputes, reconsider our mistakes, multiply our efforts and solidarity in a europe which will ultimately and finally unite.' the untiring energy of the martyrs and the heroes of 1956, the remembrance of the people, have maintained this faith and strength. the big task for us now is to join the european union. that includes everything that our peaceful revolution of 1989-1990 meant and still means to us: intellectual, legal and political reconstruction, transformation of the economy, the catching-up process that has been going on for the past 12 or 13 years. the road is difficult, the pace is tremendous. there is a lot of joy and success, there are lots of sacrifices and achievements. but we had no choice but to follow our hearts and interests and catch up with the european union as soon as possible. the european union enlargement process is a historical opportunity for us in hungary. but it is historical for you too. however, it does make a difference where the frontiers of the european union will run. we are convinced that without us a united europe would be just a political torso. europe was always weakened when the centre was pushed towards the west and cut off from the rest of europe. and now the dictates of history and the will of the european union are clear to us: the central and east european countries are to be admitted as members of the european union. now, for the first time, we can say with great certainty that hungary will be a member of the eu in the foreseeable future. the european commission's 2002 report on hungary's progress towards accession and the strategy paper evaluating the candidate countries listed hungary amongst those countries that can conclude the accession negotiations before the end of this year and join the european union in 2004. the positive outcome of the referendum in ireland removed another obstacle in the way of enlargement. i would like to take this opportunity to express my appreciation to the irish people for their responsible decision. for us, the importance of accession goes well beyond just political, economic, financial and administrative integration. we wish to become a member country in a community built on common european values, values which have nourished our civilisation for thousands of years. but we have to fight for them every day. we are indebted to the citizens of our countries; we must make sure that they become citizens of the european union on the basis of equality. the equal dignity of all human beings must stand at the centre of european values. a common europe bears the same responsibility for all the citizens of europe – for us hungarians, too. popular support for hungary's accession to the european union is very high in our country today. surveys and polls predict a 70-80% 'yes' vote. hungarian citizens have a very positive picture of europe and want hungary to be an equal member in the community of european nations. the unification of europe is not just a political slogan. we believe that unity must be reflected in the conditions of accession as well. it is very important for us to join the european union, but it is also important to do so under fair conditions. to be more specific, no policy can prevail for long if it differentiates between old and new members, for example in agriculture, direct payments or the allocation of financial resources. we must create the appropriate conditions so that hungarian citizens feel the advantages of membership from the very first moment, and see better and better opportunities for catching up. (applause)speaking of equality, may i just mention a problem of which i am sure you are well aware. as a matter of fact, we do enjoy the support of the european parliament on this matter. on the basis of population, hungary is entitled to 22, not 20, seats in the european parliament after accession, although the treaty of nice suggests 20. if it is less than 22, the principle of proportional representation would be infringed. (applause) equality for all citizens in europe also means that everyone must be considered a member, without discrimination. the poor and those people living on the margins of society are also part of the eu. europe must not exclude one single person. everyone must be integrated, regardless of social and cultural background. hungary wants to enhance the europe of solidarity. we hungarians also have a lot to do in this field. our special responsibility is to improve the social conditions of the underprivileged roma population in hungary, and promote their social integration. this is a task of historical magnitude. in the past few years, hungarian governments have taken important steps towards improving the institutional, financial and social conditions of the roma. but we know we have to trying to evade our responsibility, but we do count on european experience and support. good solutions wherever we find them could serve as a model for other european countries struggling with similar problems. enlargement will bring advantages not only to new member states, but also to the current member states of the union and their citizens. the symbolic power behind the peaceful and democratic markets expand. european division and uncertainty will be replaced by stability and overall security. opportunities will be opened up for settling disputes peacefully. the different ethnic communities will have a better chance of living together in harmony. so the union will have enormous economic, political and social potential to combat the harmful effects of globalisation. the hungarian participants in the european convention are faced more and more with the question of what kind of european union hungary will be joining. hungary is ready to keep going on the road to integration, in writing. - it would be the last thing that "events" (incidents, accidents just avoided, etc.) occurring in european civil aviation are brought to the attention of all the member states of the european union, which is not the case at present. however, while the report calls for these events to be recorded and communicated to the states, it also calls for the 'confidentiality' of information on them to be guaranteed. but to whom and to what purpose can such secrecy be used, if not to conceal the reality from airport workers, passengers and air transport staff, if not to safeguard the commercial and financial interests of airlines? on the contrary, we need the greatest possible transparency, and first of all complete transparency vis-à-vis the people. for this is the only way to update the whole chain of responsibility in the "events" in question. this chain of responsibility must be traced back to the top, i.e. to the direct and ultimate responsible parties, the airlines and airport managing companies. we therefore abstain on this report.
in writing. - the rapporteur calls for the european parliament to have access to documents on security and defence classified as 'confidential', 'secret' or 'top secret', while stating that these documents are 'not accessible to the public' and therefore hidden from the people of the european union, even though the latter claims to ensure their defence and security. this only underlines the absurdity of this claim and the hypocrisy of the european institutions, which never miss an opportunity to boast of the alleged 'transparency' of their activities. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's external borders are not encroached upon by the countries of the region. clearly, in matters of security and defence, as in all other matters considered of some importance by the council and the commission, the latter inform the european parliament only to the extent that they wish to do so. this will only surprise those who imagine that the european parliament has any other role than to provide a so-called democratic cover for policies which, dictated by the interests of the ruling classes, suffer no control. we shall vote against this report and the accompanying motion for a resolution.
in writing. - the duff report, which calls for the charter of fundamental rights to be incorporated into a european constitution, was voted on by a large majority despite our opposition. if its conclusions were to be implemented at the next intergovernmental conference, it would create a contradiction at the heart of the european institutions, the negative effects of which would soon be apparent. it so happens that the day before yesterday we were discussing the fiscal stability pact, and in the end many speakers, like romano prodi, thought it was stupid because it was too rigid. what would a charter integrated into the treaties be if it were not the equivalent of a stability pact applied to political rights? we would soon see that this rigid charter is no more suited to the reality of a union of distinct peoples than the fiscal stability pact is today. so even when it sees the harmful results of rigidity, our assembly, carried away by its old distortions and its ultimate goal of superstate, always falls back into the same rut. the mpf delegation proposed a re-founding treaty for europe, which would be very different from the constitution of a super-state, as it would recognise the need for flexible relations between sovereign national democracies.
in writing. - i am one of those who welcomed the drafting, voting and proclamation of the charter of fundamental rights in the year 2000 and who welcomed it, even though we can - and i can always wish and even want to - advocate for further progress in the human, civil and social fields. a careful reading of all the articles of our charter shows the obvious interest of such a document common to the 15 of today and the 25 of tomorrow. with it, the citizens of europe have finally started to move! that is why, like the rapporteur, i am a supporter of a european constitution and would like our charter of fundamental rights to be incorporated into that constitution. this does not, of course, prevent us from being very critical of today's europe, which is too liberal economically, too subject to the financial and stock market powers, and too politically inexistent in comparison with the united states in dealing with the major world problems. however, i believe that it is with a european constitution incorporating the charter of fundamental rights that we will have the means to move forward on a path that will allow us to profoundly transform the europe of today that i am criticizing.
in writing. - i am firmly opposed to the idea of a european constitution, which presupposes the existence of a "european people" which today is totally non-existent (there are only the peoples of the member states), and i am opposed to this report. this charter, drafted under very questionable conditions, is not intended to strengthen the protection of fundamental rights in the community legal order, which is only a pretext. several instruments already exist: the case law of the ecj, the european convention on human rights, and above all, national constitutions (whose status should be thoroughly reassessed) perfectly fulfil this function. this charter has only one ambition, which is clearly stated in this report: to become the preamble to the 'true false' european constitution. the aim is to make a decisive attack on national sovereignty by means of a text which would have considerable legal value (priority status in primary law) and whose content could seriously affect the constitutional traditions of the states. moreover, by placing national constitutions, in their most essential respects, under the exclusive jurisdiction of the cjeu, the report shows an intolerable and offensive suspicion of the member states. the letter and spirit of this report are simply unacceptable.

- madam president, on my return from the un mission to bosnia-herzegovina, i remember being received in brussels in the autumn of 1993 by manfred werner, then secretary-general of nato, and giving a firm impression that the alliance should prepare to engage in the balkans or give up its existence. the argument i developed then is easy to transpose today. in the post-cold war period, was the alliance able to engage in the major crisis developing in the heart of europe, or were european citizens led to ask themselves what it could still be used for, and whether it was worth continuing to invest a share of their tax dollars in it? it took two long years and the tragedy of the fall of srebrenica for this message to be heard. but on 31 august 1995, by supporting the action of the un reaction force deployed on mount igman to silence the serbian batteries that had resumed the indiscriminate bombing of the city of sarajevo, the alliance played a vital part in the solution of the crisis, enabling the signing of the dayton agreements and the establishment of a definitive ceasefire. since then, the alliance has successfully re-engaged in kosovo and more recently in macedonia, helping to restore calm, although it has not solved all political problems. today, the same debate is raging over the role that the atlantic alliance might play in the fight against international terrorism. the alliance is in crisis, as the americans have not felt the need to call on its organization in the war in afghanistan. does the unilateralism thus manifested mean the death of the alliance? i do not believe that, since the americans themselves have made the observation and expressed the wish. the alliance's vocation remains to intervene within and around european territory, wherever there is a threat to its values, those just mentioned by my friend pacheco pereira. international terrorism is one of them, and it is a major one. to this end, the only way to reform nato and ensure its survival is to finally build a europe of defence. the alternative is simple: either the european union continues to leave the military problems of its continent to the americans, content to deal more or less with the problems of peace, thus playing the role of the athenians of ancient rome, or it finally commits itself resolutely to their side to share with them the burden of defending it against all threats, as they have constantly asked us to do since the origins of the atlantic alliance.

mr president, the existence and development of an agricultural sector are vital questions for the countries of the south. their potential in this area is often very high. ambitious land reforms are being or should be undertaken in these countries. but above all, the question is whether they can feed themselves. i therefore want to support my group's request from the outset that the right to food sovereignty, in other words the right of peoples to define their own policy, be recognised in a specific united nations convention. developing countries are often limited to the export of a few unprocessed products. the evidence is that export specialization around raw materials is not very helpful and weakens economies by subjecting them to the vagaries of world markets. moreover, the destruction of traditional food crops by export monocultures benefits almost exclusively multinational firms. moreover, as the report rightly points out, uncontrolled global free trade is having a devastating effect on agriculture in the south. the opening up of agricultural markets requires farmers to produce at international market prices. the prices are so low that neither the farmers of the north nor those of the south can produce in an environmentally friendly way and earn enough to support their families. in these circumstances, as an ngo in burkina faso put it, how can we make it appear that international trade is the key to the development of the countries of the south? the northern countries have always protected their agriculture. why should what worked and still works for the north not work for the south? the opening up must therefore benefit farmers or multinational companies which buy up, for example, the banana plantations in cameroon or côte d'ivoire. allowing developing countries to safeguard their fundamental right to food security and the survival of their peasantry therefore implies bringing clear principles into international negotiations, starting with the recognition, at the wto level, of preferential and differential treatment for developing countries, treatment which must be interpreted with this objective in mind. the european union cannot continue to defend the development of the countries of the south and at the same time pursue an agricultural policy which ruins many of their efforts in this sector. it is therefore essential to speed up the abolition of export subsidies granted by the union, just as the sharp increase in agricultural subsidies decided by the us agricultural guideline law, with subsidies amounting to 180 billion dollars over ten years, must be condemned. secondly, the eu should play a much more active role in ensuring that fair prices are set on the world market and thus prevent the deterioration of terms of trade. the weight of the debt also contributes to the increase in export crops to obtain the foreign exchange needed to repay this debt. the cancellation of the convention is therefore more important than ever. finally, and i conclude, as regards aid, there is an urgent need to invest in human resources and infrastructure, particularly in transport. the urgency is also in preserving water and biodiversity as public goods.
mr president, today, of the six billion people in the world, more than 800 million suffer from malnutrition and, of this total, three quarters are rural people, poor farmers, poorly equipped, lacking a market for their products and therefore limiting their production to their own consumption needs. it is essential to understand that the majority of those who suffer from hunger are not city dwellers buying food, but rural people selling food. so it is the fall in agricultural prices that is starving the third world. only access to markets at remunerative prices can enable these poor farmers to have sufficient monetary income to modernise their production, buy tools, access inputs, irrigation, improved seeds. the countries that have been most successful in reducing hunger, particularly india and china, are those that, through policies to support agricultural prices, input subsidies and transport and irrigation infrastructure, have been able to give their farmers access to their own internal market and thus increase their purchasing power, productivity and production. on the contrary, the countries where famines have increased are those where the fall in agricultural prices has impoverished farmers, disrupted marketing channels and pushed many rural people, driven by poverty, to the under-equipped suburbs or to emigration. it is therefore urgent to put an end to the fall in agricultural prices. access to a profitable local market is the first right of every farmer, the first condition for the growth of agricultural production, a necessity for reducing world hunger. we must abandon the crazy utopia of wanting to turn the planet into a gigantic agricultural market without frontiers. to try to compete the chadian peasant with the farmer in minnesota, or the shepherd in the andes with the landlord farmer in new zealand, simply does not make sense. the countries which are the proponents of this global single market, particularly those of the cairns group, are not countries of hunger but countries which, thanks to particularly low production costs, large areas, low wages and advanced agricultural investments, are capable of ruining the agriculture of countries which do not have these advantages. as far as the policies of the european union are concerned, three conclusions must be drawn. firstly, all the agricultural development projects we finance in developing countries must include a component of aid to bring food products to market. secondly, we must help developing countries, or groups of countries with similar production costs, to protect their domestic market against the dumping of world prices by means of instruments without which their producers will be ruined. thirdly, we must exert all our influence in international trade negotiations to ensure that the right to agricultural exceptionalism is recognized, the right of nations to protect their farmers who feed them. the amendments proposed by our committee on agriculture were in this direction. they were adopted by the development committee, and i invite you to support them.
in writing. - subsidies to large european farms are a handicap for our small-scale production, but also for those of developing countries which are not equipped to face such competition. the cap must be revised in this respect, adding all the measures which are likely to enable these countries to develop a competitive agriculture in terms of production costs and product quality. the environment will therefore be respected so that its degradation does not lead to the degradation of arable land, in particular in relation to intensive crops, the intensive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, and the pollution of agricultural products by gmos. in this way we can preserve a healthy and organic production. particular attention will be given to these issues, in particular through collaboration with the joint research centre. the conservation and rational use of water resources is also of the utmost importance for these countries. the smap, meda and all other cooperation programmes between the european union and third countries could also be developed in this direction.

- ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i would like to begin my speech on the transeuropean energy networks by emphasizing once again that energy is not a commodity like any other and that the market cannot be its main regulatory element. the security of energy supplies is a condition for the political independence of our countries and of europe. this security requires diversification of energy sources and it implies heavy investments in the long term, if not in the very long term. energy is also an important element of spatial planning and is fully integrated into the field of public services in the noblest sense of the term. i would add that we must always bear in mind, when we talk about energy and transport networks, that while there is new infrastructure to be created, there is also existing infrastructure to be re-developed to make better use of it. finally, we must have - and i say this emphatically - an obsession with the environment in all its dimensions: visual dimension, pollution, depletion of resources, not to mention the issue of waste. i can also say, with regard to the report by mr beysen, whom i congratulate on his work, that i fully agree with the proposals put forward. the energy transmission networks must be improved and completed and the less profitable networks must be supported where they are useful, by means of studies and investment. the internal energy market is necessary, but more than deregulation, its implementation requires investment throughout the union, especially in the less accessible and less dense regions. the interconnection of networks is necessary, no one disputes that. but we must not forget that energy is needed to put in these networks, and therefore a number of conditions must be met. finally, i would like to confirm the importance for us of renewable energy, of research in this field and of the public investment effort required for their development. i must confess that i do not quite understand the link some people want to make between this objective of developing renewable energy and a liberal logic which often leads to the search for the lowest cost in the short term, without concern for the consequences in the medium and long term. in conclusion, while i criticise the liberal principles which i consider to be dangerous for europe's energy independence and for small consumers, not to mention the less favoured regions, i think that the commission's guidelines on transeuropean networks are going in the right direction and i should like to thank you for that, madam commissioner.

commission. – mr president and mr purvis, i know one thing and that is that the gmo issue will give me grey hairs. we know from eurobarometer opinion polls that most people are worried about gmos. at the same time, they say that they do not know enough about them. perhaps there is a connection. i would like to say to mrs breyer that we have looked at those concerns very carefully to ensure that we establish clear legislation – a clear framework – for handling both the potential benefits and the risks of gmos. that is why we have revised directive 18/2001/ec to include better risk assessment and better information, so that consumers can make an informed choice. that is why we have proposed further legislation on traceability and labelling. however, it would not be honest to say that if we continue to import seeds, for example, we can guarantee total purity and no adventitious presence of gmos. we know that everything in nature escapes – through cross-pollination for example – so closing borders is not a viable solution. we have to be pragmatic and establish levels and thresholds to deal with natural phenomena. we have to look at the situation as it actually is and at the products we import. this leads me to mr trakatellis' question about traceability. the proposals on traceability and labelling, as well as on food and feed, are not based entirely on the detectability of gmos. even if they cannot be detected, consumers have the right to know. the current novel foods regulation will be replaced by these proposals and the scope will be broadened to give consumers a choice, even if the gmos are not detectable. consumers have the right to be informed of the presence of gmos in the products they buy, even if the gmos are not detectable. i shall comment on two further issues that have been raised. firstly, on labelling thresholds, the commission can only take account of existing legislation and, for the time being, a 1% threshold is in force for foodstuffs. this 1% threshold is provided for by the council regulation, as amended by commission regulation (ec) no 49/2000. above that 1% threshold, an indication of the presence of a genetic modification in a food is compulsory. as the recital of the regulation states, the 1% value best serves the purpose of establishing a tolerance level which simultaneously remains low and takes into account the necessary feasibility along the production chain. all these factors along the production chain are involved. the seeds thresholds are based on this 1% threshold. you have to count backwards in order to reach this 1% threshold. a recital of the draft commission directive on seeds provides that, should the food threshold change, the thresholds for seeds would need to be reconsidered accordingly. on the coexistence issue, the institute for prospective technological studies is carrying out a study entitled 'scenarios for coexistence of genetically modified, conventional and organic crops in european agriculture', commissioned by the agriculture directorate-general and coordinated by the joint research centre. the main aim of the study is to assess the consequences arising from an increase in the cultivation of gm crops in the european union in the context of coexistence. the study aimed to identify the source and estimated levels of adventitious presence of gm crops in non-gm crops at farm level, identify and assess changes in farming practices that could reduce adventitious presence below policy relevant thresholds and estimate the costs of relevant changes in farming practices, monitoring systems and potential insurance systems. the study confirms that cross-pollination and coexistence are issues that need to be considered in relation to agricultural production in general. the results of the study need to be interpreted with caution. only three crops were analysed: oilseed rape for seed production, maize for feed use and potatoes for human consumption. the results are derived from models and have not been validated by real field data. therefore this study provided preliminary conclusions but the hypothetical results need to be confirmed and further research will be done. the commission is discussing this and coordinating with the various directorate-generals. this debate will certainly continue. this is a very complex and sensitive issue, legally, technically and politically. as i said earlier, we readily admit that we do not have all the answers. however, what we can do – as we have done with other technologies – is to put in place a legal framework to deal with the potential benefits as well as the risks. that is what we have tried to do with the revised directive 18/2001/ec, traceability and labelling. consequently it will, for example, affect thresholds when it comes to seed regulation. i thank you for this debate and i am sure we shall continue it at a later date.

- doc. b5-0545/2002 by mr collins, on behalf of the uen group, on the situation in nepal; - b5-0547/2002 by mr carrilho and others, on behalf of the pse group, on the situation in nepal; - b5-0550/2002 by mr vinci, on behalf of the gue/ngl group, on the situation in nepal; - b5-0555/2002 by mr mann, on behalf of the ppe-de group, on the situation in nepal; - b5-0558/2002 by mr van den bos, on behalf of the eldr group, on the political situation in nepal; - b5-0560/2002 by mr messner and others, on behalf of the v group, on nepal.
- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by expressing our solidarity with the people of nepal, who have been living through one of the most difficult periods in their history for the last few years. its young democracy is faltering, the rule of law is steadily receding into arbitrariness and violence. in less than a year, more than 3,000 people have been killed in violent clashes between the army and maoist guerrillas, whose stated aim is to overthrow the monarchy, apparently against the wishes of the people. in reality, with almost total indifference from the international community, this people have been facing a full-blown civil war for more than six years. this difficult situation has been sharply aggravated by events at the beginning of this month. by announcing the prime minister's dismissal and temporarily granting himself executive powers, an event unprecedented since the end of the absolute monarchy in 1990, king gyanendra has opened a major political crisis; the fact is that although he subsequently appointed a prime minister, he has no representation and, in fact, the temptation seems very strong on the part of the king to use the fight against the maoist guerrillas to suspend the rule of law and put an end to the exercise of parliamentary democracy that has been in force for twelve years. by destabilising nepal, these events are adding to the turmoil and instability in the entire region. the european union can no longer be satisfied with a few wishes in the face of such a situation. we must, with the greatest insistence, invite the new prime minister to resume, without preconditions, dialogue with the maoist rebels; in addition, it would be desirable in this context for the council to consider the appointment as soon as possible of a special representative for nepal, who could possibly serve as a mediator between the parties to the conflict. finally, and above all, since this conflict is largely due to economic and social difficulties, we must provide substantial financial aid to enable us to support effectively the return to peace and democracy in this small kingdom tomorrow.
commission. – mr president, together with honourable members, the commission deplores the increasing number of victims generated by the clashes between maoists and government forces in nepal. it is - mr president, madam president-in-office of the council, commissioner, i have the pleasure today of presenting to you the motion for a resolution on the mid-term reform which was adopted by the committee on agriculture on 21 october. without wishing to go into an exhaustive historical recollection of the various stages of the common agricultural policy and the successive reforms which the european union has undertaken, let me remind you that the european council, at the berlin summit, defined the guidelines applicable for the period 1999-2006. it also introduced amendments to certain common market organizations, in particular those for cereals, beef and veal and milk. i would remind you that the european council has asked the commission to present a report in 2002 on the trend in agricultural expenditure, accompanied if necessary by appropriate proposals. it is in this context that the european commission has sent parliament and the council a proposal for reform of the common agricultural policy, which commissioner fischler presented to us on 10 july. it is on this basis that the committee on agriculture has begun to reflect, and this has led to the drafting of a resolution which i have the honour to present to you today. the debate was intense. as the 388 amendments tabled by the members of the committee show, the compromise we were able to reach required an effort on the part of all, regardless of their political leanings or the national interests they were defending. and the vote, obtained by a very large majority, demonstrates, if necessary, the concern of its members to overcome political and national contingencies in order to be able to present a reflection that could influence the debates. this resolution has three objectives. firstly, it aims to recall the basic principles of the common agricultural policy, in particular financial solidarity, the need for a fair income for producers and the maintenance of border protection to avoid distortions of competition. secondly, to define the main guidelines for its implementation by taking better account of the concerns expressed by european citizens on the environment, health protection, food quality, rural development and animal welfare, while responding to farmers' demands for remuneration for their work and simplification in the implementation of the agricultural policy, so that young farmers are encouraged to settle down. finally, the cap reform should be seen in a long-term perspective, so as to give farmers and the agri-food industry more generally a better understanding of the mechanisms for managing markets and to enable them to make long-term investments. that is why the committee on agriculture feels that, without calling into question the competence of the other committees concerned, any adjustment of the cap must be in the long-term budgetary perspective, which must in any case go beyond 2006, when new guidelines will have to be negotiated. this concern is now shared by the council. and this convergence of views between the committee on agriculture and the council shows the importance of maintaining a strong common agricultural policy, which is convergent in the eyes of all our fellow citizens and which today is calling for validation. the resolution before you: first, aid for the management of markets. the european commission's approach to decoupling direct aid to producers thus simplifies the management of direct aid, but also leads to the eventual dismantling of all market management measures. that is why the committee on agriculture suggests partial decoupling. moreover, its introduction should not lead to a reduction in the prices of production. finally, the proposals for lower intervention prices suggested do not appear to be necessary in the present context. and the idea of advancing, during the committee's work, the introduction of partial decoupling would allow producers to receive a fixed basic aid per holding or per hectare, calculated on the basis of historical references but limited to a ceiling of eur 10 000. the second element of the resolution is the strengthening of the second pillar, to reinforce certain rural development policies. the resolution stresses the flexibility that is essential to the implementation of rural development policies, flexibility that allows for the consideration of concerns expressed at regional level. the third guideline concerns the need for producers receiving community aid, both those under the first and those under the second pillar, to strictly respect the principles laid down in the european directives on environmental protection and animal welfare. finally, the resolution adopted by the committee on agriculture called for the european union's position to be strengthened in the forthcoming negotiations, taking into account the dynamics of enlargement, in particular by stressing the need for coherence between the proposals for mid-term reform and the agricultural offer to the applicant countries, in order to allow for better integration of these countries, while stressing the room for manoeuvre provided by the wto negotiations. the commissioner reminded us of all this in the committee on agriculture on 5 october and the european commission should present legislative provisions in the near future which will have to meet all these constraints. we are here to analyse them, to listen to the commission when it proposes them, and we are going to take our responsibilities at parliament level. that is why i ask this house to adopt the resolution as soon as tomorrow.

- mr president, after the decisions of the brussels summit, only certain elements of our earlier debate remain relevant. this is the case with those which concern the guiding principles around which a long-term cap should be structured. four principles seem to me particularly important. the first is price defence. like any other business, the farm must live primarily from the sale of its products and not from the taxpayers' aid, which is always precarious and revocable. it needs remunerative prices which must also take into account the cost of environmental, social, quality and safety requirements, which are those of our fellow citizens. this logic of coupling is becoming fully relevant again after the brussels summit capped the budget for direct aids at a level that does not even guarantee compensation for inflation. unless a significant drop in agricultural income is accepted, in particular from 2007, this erosion cannot be compensated by anything other than prices which ensure, as provided for in article 33 of the treaty, a fair standard of living for the agricultural population. that is the starting point for negotiations at the wto, not the other way around. the second principle is a new definition of community preference based on the disparity between the requirements imposed on european producers and those imposed on third countries. this asymmetry legitimizes the protection of our internal market against social or environmental dumping on the world market. the third principle is that of stability. we can't have fun radically changing the rules of the game every three years. a farmer, and in particular a young farmer, needs, like any entrepreneur, sufficient visibility to make strategic choices and make investments with a lifespan of at least 15 years, and sometimes for his entire career. the fourth and final principle is food security. it is not enough to proclaim it, but it is necessary to put it into practice. an economic entity such as the european union must not be heavily dependent on imports, as is the case today with the strategic sector of animal protein. the disastrous blair house agreements, which gave the americans absolute domination of the oil and protein sector, should be the main concern of a commission which would really defend european interests. at the moment, mr president, we are far from that.

the rapporteur. - mr president, my remarks will be in full harmony with those of the commissioner, but i will try not to repeat myself. it is therefore a directive which aims to improve safety and which, as is unfortunately the custom, improves things after a series of accidents. the point is simple: these are ships, and when there is a breakdown, these ships must be at the disposal of the rescuers for as long as possible so that as many lives as possible can be saved. studies and experience show that this requires the maximum amount of water on a bridge. the imo, the international maritime organization, obviously took an early interest in these issues and concluded a convention called solas in 1990 for a certain water height - but i will not go into the technical details - stating that all ships had to comply with this convention and its standards by 1 october 2010. however, in september 1994, in northern europe, as you may recall, there was the estonia disaster, which killed 800 people. after the disaster, eight northern european countries, seven eu countries and norway came together and adopted stricter standards than those of the 1990 convention to prevent shipwrecks. the question for the commission and for us was what to do once these new standards were introduced, whether to extend them to the whole of the union or whether to maintain a distinction between the north and the south of the union. after carrying out the studies, technical and financial studies, the commission proposed, and it did well, to extend these standards to the whole of the union under the conditions just set out by the commissioner. so it's going to be done. it is considered possible, it is considered reasonable and it is considered to be an acceptable cost for the companies. in this way, there will be no difference between passengers who will take the boats in the north and those who will take the boats in the south. of course, a number of ships have been brought up to the so-called solas standards quite recently. so asking them to adopt such a directive is like asking them to start over. the question then arises of when, at what time and on what date the final deadline is to be set. in a spirit of compromise that everyone will understand, the commission, the council and parliament have agreed to stop all this by 2015. that is the meaning of the proposed essential amendment. the commission is also proposing a number of other amendments which will allow for adoption at first reading. i will therefore advise my colleagues, and i think my colleague mr ripoll will do the same, to resolve this matter as soon as possible, which is not a major political problem, and to ensure that all vessels and companies operating in waters governed by union law comply with the standards as soon as possible. thus the risk of accidents and loss of life will be minimized, even if the zero risk does not exist in our society.
- mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the report to be put to the vote tomorrow deals first with the balance sheet of cohesion policy. we must welcome the positive impact of this policy, which has proved indispensable to the harmonious development of the union. however, there is still work to be done. it seems that our aim should be to make this policy smarter, simpler and more generous. by smarter, i mean that this policy must be flexible and take account of the wide variety of handicaps faced by europe's regions. clearer award criteria and possible objectives need to be defined. as such, gdp statistics have a clear advantage. however, this is a convenient solution, necessarily partial and not adapted to all the realities of the field. other equally relevant and quantifiable indicators, such as accessibility, public infrastructure equipment and employment rates, must be taken into account. such an approach would make it possible to develop a cohesion policy for regions lagging behind in their development, but which is also adapted to mountain regions, sparsely populated regions and other regions with geographical handicaps. the new regional policy must also be simpler. this means that it must be easy to use by all its beneficiaries. we have started work with commissioner barnier and the member states to this end, but the current exercise has limitations which are within the framework of the regulations in force. further administrative simplification will be needed after 2006. the third ambition is to make cohesion policy more generous. today, the argument of absorptive capacity is often used to justify a limitation of the allocations granted. i believe that after 2006, if we can imagine instruments that are adapted to local needs and are easy to use, the budget for this can and should be higher. the problem is not that there is a cake to be shared among the regions, as some suggest. for all its citizens, the union must be ambitious in demonstrating that it is a space of solidarity.

- mr president, it is true that we have been diverted to mulhouse and that many of us arrive by bus. so please forgive the difficulties i may have in this intervention. what surprises me about competition and pluralism is that we are basically asking the question from two totally different and opposite points of view. on the one hand, we are looking at our countries, our member states, where competition can reach very high proportions, particularly in italy, as everyone here knows. on the other hand, we can raise the question of pluralism and competition, and from the point of view of some of the candidate countries, we can even raise the question of a single source of information to the detriment of the pluralism claimed here, since until now it can be thought that the media coverage in these countries depended exclusively on this single source. these two extremes of the competition question are therefore completely opposite. it is these two limits that we must take into account if we are to seek a balance between pluralism and a certain degree of concentration. the balance is a delicate one, but it is also a delicate one because - and i think this has not been said enough so far - it is a matter of public service. so it's not just about competition from private media, because this problem also affects the public service, and we need to achieve this balance between the two. to achieve such a balance, the commission may have to reverse its indecision on a necessary directive, which has been called for by parliament for several years. the commission must also re-examine the situation of the media, which has changed profoundly in recent years. the last study on this subject was carried out in 1994. we therefore ask the commission to take note of the new difficulties and to propose a directive. perhaps it is also worth stressing that there is a protocol to the amsterdam treaty on the system of public broadcasting in the member states. the protocol is an extract from the treaty of amsterdam which, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, provides for the competence of the member states to define and organise these tasks and for their financing, provided that this does not impede competition. so here too, it is the state aid which is obviously important and which must be emphasized and preserved. that is why it seems to all of us here today, and to my group in particular, that it is necessary to review the need for a directive. the question of media coverage cannot be avoided without also considering the content. it is clear that there is a specificity of the market and competition, a specificity which is linked to content, creation and, in particular, also to publishing. i would remind you of the french situation - which worries us - of a concentration of the publishing market in the newly established markets. this specificity deserves to be taken into account and the urgency of such a situation also needs to be stressed. in conclusion, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we hope that the convention will respect what the charter says about pluralism and that it will be able to defend this pluralism.
- mr president, the question of media pluralism is an important one, which touches the very heart of the values on which our european commitment is based, and for reasons which are obviously in the minds of all of us. without pluralism, there is no counter-power, there is no freedom and, therefore, no democracy. without pluralism, the freedom of audiovisual and cinematographic creation would be jeopardized and thus europe's cultural identity would be threatened. it is therefore essential to ensure that the principles of media diversity, pluralism and independence are applied in the member states as well as in the candidate countries. media pluralism concerns the dissemination of information, television and the internet as much as audiovisual creation. in a constantly changing media landscape, the presence of public service and private television stations and the limitation of merger and acquisition operations between commercial operators are essential guarantees for the maintenance of audiovisual pluralism and cultural diversity. similarly, we must ensure the diversification of public and private information sources across all media. the commission should therefore draw up a report on the situation of the media in general for each candidate country and for each member state. a green paper on this subject was drawn up in 1997. today, the evolution of communication technologies, the large place of the internet in information, cable television are all elements that push us to look again at the problem of media concentration. for example, it is very important that the commission should address as soon as possible the problems raised by the lack of transparency in the allocation of television licences in the member states and in the candidate countries. the european commission will then be able to decide, if necessary, to lay down rules of competition in a regulatory manner that guarantees media pluralism. freedom of speech is fragile. it can only be guaranteed by the existence of a real plurality of media, which we must all regularly monitor. - mr president, although not enough, mr medina ortega's report has the merit of going back on the decision to repeal the 1997 tobacco directive, and we welcome that. tobacco, which kills hundreds of europeans every day, is a scourge which we must combat in the name of protecting the health of our fellow citizens. we cannot be satisfied with half measures. either tobacco is a deadly poison and every effort should be made to reduce its use or even to eradicate it altogether, or tobacco is wrongly regarded as a common consumer good and there is no need for legislation. it is the persistence of this inconsistency, which mr matten has pointed out, that leads us to say that our parliament is supporting the cultivation of a product which it otherwise suppresses. the text tabled by mr medina is a step in the right direction, but the amendments proposed weaken it considerably and we will reject them. it is a good thing because it has been shown that the ban on advertising has a downward effect on tobacco consumption and that there is indeed a link between advertising and overconsumption. the amendments, oddly enough, focus on crossborder problems. for example, some seem to find virtues in borders for economic reasons, whereas in many cases it is the same people who, without caring about the consequences, advocate a wide opening of these same borders. today, with so much knowledge about the dangers of tobacco, it would be criminal not to try to dissuade younger and younger consumers from becoming addicted to a product that is advertised as having health benefits. neglect, indifference and lack of political courage in public health matters are the premises of crimes against humanity. it was this irresponsible laxity that led to the scandal of tainted blood in france and mad cow disease in britain. today, no one can say that he does not know and everyone is responsible. that is why we will support mr medina's report.
the commission has already made a number of proposals. financial conglomerates can create entirely new risk constellations, and this obviously requires action. some european countries, such as the united kingdom and sweden, have already gained good experience with general financial supervision. the general financial supervision allows equal risks to be treated equally. this is a step towards greater competitive neutrality in the financial markets. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be able to take a decision on the application of the directive in the case of a concentration. financial markets around the world have become more closely aligned. this was evident when the economic downturn was transferred from america to europe by the financial markets more quickly and more strongly than even experts expected. the same is true of financial market crises as of economic downturns: neither is now a regional problem. the objective of the supervision of financial conglomerates is to increase the stability of international financial and capital markets. however, it must be borne in mind that this cannot be achieved by a scheme confined to the territory of the european union. i think the directive will lead to a debate in the member states on 'correct implementation' because in many cases it does not provide for specific rules but gives national supervisory authorities a wide margin of discretion. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the directive is implemented in a uniform manner. the resulting national supervisory burden or relief for financial conglomerates is highly relevant for competition. finally, i would like to express my concern that the committee on supervision, by regulating the details, is ultimately shaping the content of supervisory law and that the will of parliament is therefore losing its importance.
madam president, the european council is rightly concerned about the collapse of the cyber economy, the financial scandals and the resulting deterioration of the situation. the people who should be most concerned are those who have already been dismissed or are about to be dismissed from the companies concerned, even though they are not to blame for the anarchy of your economy, which is as unjust as it is irrational. but in the face of this real evil, the only remedy we are offered is to strengthen prudential rules or improve control, as if financial conglomerates could be controlled from above by the political powers responsible for protecting them. the report also stresses the need to ensure that the directive is not used to create a situation where the financial conglomerates are threatened by the mere mention of the word 'control'. well, let those who pretend to believe that a few prudential rules and a few coordinators without real power can cure the capitalist economy of speculation, scandals and financial crises, let them vote for this report. even a vote by the european parliament cannot turn a weak recommendation into a magic potion against the ills of capitalism. your economy, based on the pursuit of private profit and competition, is even more unpredictable than the weather, because if we can predict the weather three days in advance, who can predict the stock market overnight? by voting against this text we express our opposition to a stupid economic order which is dangerous for society.

- the next item is the joint debate on the following reports: - report (a5-0380/2002) by mr stevenson, on behalf of the committee on fisheries, on the communication from the commission on the reform of the common fisheries policy (implementation schedule) (com (2002) 181 - c5-0330/2002 - 2002/2174 (cos)) - report (a5-0360/2002) by mr souchet, on behalf of the committee on fisheries, on the communication from the commission setting out a community action plan for the integration of environmental protection requirements into the common fisheries policy (com (2002) 1862) (c5-0331/2002 - 2002/2175 (cos))
the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, as we approach the decisive dates for the future of the cfp, with the redefinition of its objectives and procedures, it seems to me important that our parliament should be able to affirm forcefully the five principles which have served as the guiding principle of my report and which your committee on fisheries has wanted to emphasize with a view to fully integrating the requirements of environmental protection into the new common fisheries policy. the first principle is that nothing can be done without the fishermen. fisheries and maritime professionals are the first to be concerned by the protection of the marine environment and the first to be aware of the need to safeguard it. they are also the first victims of its deterioration, as the new black tide that is now destroying the fishermen of galicia unfortunately attests. three years after the erika disaster in the vendée and brittany, it should not have been possible for the 'prestige', a garbage ship, to be allowed into community waters. our report stresses the need for rapid and rigorous implementation of the package of directives, specifically erika i and erika ii. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fishermen are not caught by the fishermen themselves, but by the fishermen themselves. the second principle is that decisions on the management of fish stocks should be based on as sound and accurate scientific knowledge as possible. the economic and social consequences of these decisions are so far-reaching that it is unacceptable that they should be taken lightly. i therefore welcome the fact that the committee on fisheries has accepted the request to instruct the european commission to draw up a specific action plan to improve the current very weak system of stock assessment by integrating practical, empirical and pragmatic knowledge of fishermen alongside landing controls and by placing the interdisciplinary nature of biological and socioeconomic sciences at the very heart of the process of drawing up scientific advice. the third principle proposes that flexible and reversible management instruments such as tacs and quotas should be used to adjust levies to the available resource at all times, rather than brutal and irreversible instruments with dramatic social effects such as ship-wrecking. the fourth principle calls for priority to be given to improving fishing gear and techniques, with a view to ensuring that discards, by-catches and impacts on habitats are reduced. of course, such measures cannot be adopted in a uniform and centralised manner. they must leave a large part to the initiatives of the professional circles. fishermen, their professional associations and the territorial authorities of the coast must be granted the right to experiment. initiatives in this field should be recognised and encouraged. the atlantic coast is thus experiencing some very promising developments. i will give as examples those aimed at adapting fishing vessels and gear to collect macrodescombrants or hydrocarbon beds, or the development of artificial reefs to facilitate the development of breeding and resting areas for marine life, or assisted fertilisation techniques at sea for cod. my report proposes that such experiments should be eligible for public funding. the fifth principle states that public aid for fleet modernisation, which aims to improve working conditions, safety on board, energy savings and product quality, is perfectly compatible with the protection of the marine environment. i am glad that the committee on fisheries has largely followed my proposal and has adopted all these positive and constructive proposals, thus rejecting the very negative view of fishing activity which was so strongly permeated by the european commission's communication. i hope that by voting massively in favour of this report, parliament will make it clear to everyone that the protection of the marine environment must be done with the fishermen and not against them. that is why, instead of being accusatory, instead of talking incessantly about declining activity and palliative policy, your committee on fisheries has preferred to send a message of confidence and hope to the professionals to strengthen their growing respect for the quality of the marine environment, which is one of the important objectives that the new common fisheries policy must pursue.
- madam president, i wanted to say a few words about the struan stevenson report. i am glad that he is calling for the continuation of the system of access to water and resources and the fundamental principle of relative stability. i regret, however, that mr nogueira's original proposal, which sought to put the economic and social dimension of the common fisheries policy back on the agenda and, therefore, to examine it together with the question of fishing effort, was not adopted. what i note is that the european commission's proposal on the timetable for reform of the common fisheries policy reflects the non-priority it gives to the social consequences of its project, since they appear only in the seventh row of the proposed measures. as for the commission communication of 6 november on palliative care linked to the reform, it confirms the planned destruction of 28 000 jobs over three years, between 2003 and 2006, due to the massive shipwrecking as envisaged by the commission. we reserve the right, of course, to ask the commissioner about these dramatic figures when the time comes, madam president, when we are considering this communication.

fisheries sector. i am sorry to say that this funding will be reduced somewhat in the coming years, but we are prepared to allocate more funds within the whole of fisheries research to this specific purpose, namely the study of the state of stocks and their development. we also want to increase research into alternative technical measures, such as the development of new fishing gear. but let's commission, but by the member states. the commission has only observer status. but the scientists tell us that in recent years, the reports on landings, on the composition of the catch, have sometimes simply been wrong, that there have been false reports, and therefore wrong conclusions. i don't want to accuse anyone here, but we have to at least acknowledge that this is a problem that we also have concepts. these concepts must be adapted to the fisheries and fishing activities and stocks concerned and we must respect the precautionary principle. these concepts must also ensure that discards are minimised. but mr stevenson, it is not so simple that you can only say that the quota system is to blame for the rejections. there are other concepts in other countries around the world that don't have quotas and have a similar discard problem. the fact that these discards continue to occur has to do with all the essential components of fishing. there is certainly a technical aspect to the gear which is not very selective. there is certainly a problem in mixed fisheries, that some stocks are quota-filled earlier than others. this will even lead to the discarding of stocks that we do not want at all. but there is also, of course, the problem of limiting fishing effort. i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has been unable to reach a decision on the matter. the mediterranean also features in your report in a large part. i agree with you that the mediterranean needs to be treated differently. this is also part of tailor-made concepts. we cannot use the same methods that work in the north sea: the mediterranean is different because of the types of fishing that take place there - mainly artisanal fishing. it's different because of the narrow continental shelf that we find there. it is different because of the much greater participation of third countries in the fisheries there. we need a specific approach to this. we have submitted one. temporarily is also a legal question. i warn you not to say we're voting. we need a permanent arrangement. the european court of justice will then decide what is legal. i think that the treaty should expiring, but this means that these countries will also have access to the northern waters. i know very well what is being said here, namely the question of the back-firing. in particular, the problem is that when species are caught without tacs and quotas, other species subject to quotas are also caught, and there is a risk that fish which are in themselves very valuable are caught and thrown back commission. – madam president, i wish to begin by thanking the rapporteur, mr di lello finuoli, for his very comprehensive and helpful report on the two danish initiatives on confiscation. first, i shall address the framework decision on the confiscation of crime-related proceeds, instrumentalities and property. as the rapporteur said, it is essential that all member states adopt rules providing for confiscation in general. the added value of this initiative, however, is that it addresses extended powers to confiscate the property of a person convicted of a serious crime, especially when the convicted person was involved in organised crime. the problems that this initiative raises, as the rapporteur has said, are mainly concerned with the idea of extended powers of confiscation which consist essentially of extending confiscation measures to property which is not linked to the crime for which the person has been convicted, permitting confiscation of property belonging to a convicted person if the person cannot prove that he obtained the property through legitimate means, and permitting confiscation of property belonging to the spouse of the convicted person. in my view, it should be possible to break the link between the offence for which the person has been convicted and the property to be confiscated, especially if that property is itself of illegal origin. however, the scope of application should be limited to serious offences linked to organised crime. in addition, it is not the relationship between the convicted person and the third party which is important, but the fact that illegally obtained property was transferred to a third person. so, like the rapporteur, i agree with the general approach adopted by the danish presidency. i also support most of the amendments by the rapporteur, in particular the amendment which introduced the notion of proportionality, so that confiscation does not result in a loss of property disproportionate to the offence committed; and the amendment which limits the scope of application of extended powers of confiscation to organised crime. i have some doubts about the amendment the rapporteur has just mentioned, which demands that member states avoid a reversal of the burden of proof in their legislation. i sincerely do not see the need to include such a provision in this specific instrument on confiscation as this could be interpreted as conflicting with the principle of subsidiarity. the danish initiative envisages a certain flexibility concerning the burden of proof. in this area, as mr di lello finuoli mentioned, we have to find the correct balance between combating organised crime on the one hand and on the other respecting the fundamental rights of the accused. it is not necessary, therefore, to reverse the burden of proof. however, we should consider the fact that the person convicted in connection with organised crime who cannot justify his lifestyle should face the prospect of confiscation of property unless this person demonstrates that he obtained the property by legitimate means. as for the second danish initiative for a framework decision on the execution in the european union of confiscation orders, this second initiative deals, as mr marinho has just said, with the mutual recognition and execution of confiscation orders in the european union. it is closely connected with the initiative that has been presented on the freezing and confiscation of property, for which mr marinho was the rapporteur, and the commission intends to maintain the overall coherence between the two initiatives. some of the issues raised by the second initiative are now under negotiation in the council, with regard also to the framework decision concerning the mutual recognition of financial penalties. we are therefore pleased that the rapporteur shares the positive view of the commission on this framework decision. most of your amendments seek to ensure that decisions are recognised only when issued by judges. we agree that it is important to be clear about the status of the issuing authority. the initial text as you have mentioned confused judicial authorities, courts and judges. this needs to be ratified. we support your view that it is not appropriate for orders issued by investigating magistrates and prosecutors to fall within the scope of these instruments. the rapporteur also suggests that the issuing state should be prohibited from imposing a custodial sentence as an alternative to confiscation. although we agree with the objective of this amendment, it seems to us that this issue might be better addressed in the first framework decision on the approximation of national rules on confiscation. i would conclude by thanking the rapporteur and also the house for its patience during this late-night debate.

- mr president, i would like to make three points. as regards the enlargement to include turkey, it is normal that there should be a debate. we cannot both lament the fact that europeans are losing interest in europe and at the same time refuse to discuss enlargement, which would take us further away from the original project of european union. at the same time, the enlargement we are now carrying out is the one which includes the largest number of countries. let us remember that we have never expanded to more than three countries at a time. this enlargement is not yet complete. we all wish him success. let us first succeed before we start discussing possible future enlargements. we must be able to propose to our major neighbours in the european union, including turkey - but not the only one - an alternative solution to the dilemma in which we are being locked: membership or exclusion. but there is another solution, as the epp proposes, which is much better suited to the problem. it is the definition of a specific framework of relations with a substantial economic component and with the possibility of financing a number of projects and infrastructures: this is how the north american continent is organized, and no one there is proposing to bring mexico or canada into the united states of america. the epp opens up a new way of thinking, much more adapted to the facts of the problem. i am sure that the european parliament will listen to the people's wishes and ask for progress in this direction and for a new framework between the european union and the countries of its immediate neighbourhood.

enormous task of completing the negotiations with each of the 10 candidate countries. the presidency will conduct the negotiations in cooperation with the commission in full respect of the eu rules on the expenditure ceilings set in berlin and the conclusions adopted in brussels. that is what the general affairs council recommended to the presidency at its meeting yesterday. the presidency will work actively on this basis and will do its utmost to find compromises acceptable to both the new and the existing member states. however, it requires a great deal of compromise and a great deal of understanding of the other party's views and needs. the negotiating situation is one where, of course, negotiations can take place and flexibility can be shown, but i think everyone in this chamber lunch, that it is not a question of the 15 countries now writing a new treaty which the 10 new countries then agree to without having had any influence on it. the ministers meeting yesterday reaffirmed what is stated in paragraph 23 of the treaty of nice, namely that the new countries will participate in the forthcoming intergovernmental conference on a basis of full equality, with the right to speak and vote on a completely equal footing with the existing member states. that is the case, and anything else would be reprehensible, unacceptable and impossible for the politicians of the new member states to put to a referendum. i think it was mrs myller who raised the question of the new neighbours. we are getting new neighbours to the east after enlargement, and yesterday the strategy towards each of these new neighbours with a view to promoting democracy and economic reform, sustainable development and trade, and to promoting stability and prosperity, etc., across the new eu frontier. it was stressed that the specific political and economic circumstances of each country should be taken into account and that all this should be seen in the context of the ongoing deepening of cooperation with russia. and then there is talk of crossborder cooperation, of organised crime, of illegal immigration and regional cooperation between the new neighbouring countries. so
