secretary-general presented a comprehensive proposal for a solution to the cyprus conflict. it is a complex and comprehensive proposal, covering 150 pages. the plan presented is designed as a comprehensive political solution to ensure that a united cyprus can join the eu. as regards accession, the helsinki conclusions continue to form the basis of the eu's position. the eu would prefer that a reunified island join, but a solution is not a necessary prerequisite. the council will decide on the admission of cyprus taking into account all relevant factors. the eu also supports the efforts of the un secretary-general and will be able to support a comprehensive settlement of the conflict in accordance with the principles on which the eu is founded, namely that cyprus as a member state will be able to speak with one voice and ensure the proper application of eu law. as regards relations with turkey, these relations will be based on the decision of the european council, also held in helsinki. turkey is a candidate country which will be treated in exactly the same way as the other candidate countries. the commission report concluded that the political criterion for opening negotiations had not yet been met, but that considerable progress had been made. the economic criteria must be met at the latest at the time of admission to the eu. the copenhagen european council arvidsson that we all recognise that enlargement from 15 to 25 and later to 27 or 28 member states requires a new treaty, otherwise we will have problems. that is why the convention works, and that is subsidiarity is not kept in mind. with these words, mr president, i would like to thank you warmly for this eight and a half hour debate, which marks a massive support for the great project we are undertaking. we have reason to be proud of it, and i would say 'we', because i was already involved in starting it as a member of parliament.

- mr president of parliament, mr president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, commissioners, colleagues, you have told us, mr prodi, that we are launching a new procedure which will make it possible, in the context of the preparation of the commission's legislative and work programme for 2003, to coordinate more closely between the three institutions. we would like to stress the importance of this new procedure. for the first time, parliament, the council and the commission engaged in a constructive dialogue to define a legislative programme. we are particularly keen to see this cooperation and in particular to strengthen the discussions between parliament and the commission in advance. however, while this dialogue took place last spring, it was difficult to distinguish this specific legislative programming exercise from the so-called regular meetings held throughout the year between parliamentary committees and commissioners in their respective fields of competence. in future, there will probably be a need to prepare and structure this dialogue further, including the preliminary presentation by each commissioner of a policy paper on each specific legislative area. the single document, the 'annual political strategy for 2003', presented by the commission last february, proved to be insufficient, and this situation could be seen as damaging, since 2003 is a particularly decisive year because of enlargement. i have noted, however, mr president, that you are prepared to submit monthly reports to parliament. we welcome the three political priorities set by the commission and we submit the following comments: on the first point, entitled 'successful enlargement', our main concern is the correct application of the acquis communautaire throughout the enlarged union. it is therefore essential that community law in a codified version be available in all the languages of the new member states. successful enlargement means including the environmental dimension and the objective of public health and consumer protection in all other policies, as well as taking account - as you yourself have said - of human resources and also providing an effort at innovation. finally, it is necessary to monitor the application of community legislation, and it seems necessary to help these future member states to set up the appropriate structures as soon as possible. the second point, entitled 'ensuring stability and security': the threat of terrorism is a threat to the union. we therefore welcome the measures proposed to combat this scourge. this fight is one element of a wider ambition to guarantee the union's security and safety. we therefore welcome the commission's commitment to progress in creating an area of freedom, security and justice, in which individual rights will be protected. this is the case for civil protection, food security, industry, transport, energy and land use planning, so as to take account of all aspects of public health and the environment. as regards the establishment of a european prosecutor in particular, we consider it legitimate to await the conclusions of the convention on this subject before any initiative is taken. ensuring the stability and security of the union also means defining and implementing an integrated border management system, and taking concrete and coordinated measures to combat illegal immigration. we also call on the commission to come forward swiftly with proposals on immigration and asylum policy which clearly distinguish between asylum seekers, those seeking international protection and migrant workers. on this question, our group remains concerned by the lack of will we have seen in the council. it is also important to have regular monitoring of the activities of the european union and the member states in relation to the international criminal court. the third point, 'building a sustainable and supportive economy', is that if we want to avoid the deterioration of the economic environment having a negative impact on employment, it would be desirable for the commission to be able to make proposals for a more flexible labour market, which is a necessary condition for increasing employment opportunities. we appreciate the commission's firmness on the stability pact, but we also believe that it contains various shortcomings. it is regrettable that no mention is made of the tax package in the commission's programme and that no progress has been made in the area of vat with regard to the country of origin principle. and above all, we call on the commission to go further in its thinking on the harmonization of the tax base wherever this is necessary for the proper functioning of the single market, while not proposing a system aimed solely at harmonizing rates. the tax policy of the european union must in any case aim at a reduction in general taxation and a reduction in administrative burdens. economic development also requires the strengthening of infrastructure, particularly in the field of transport. and we ask, following the court of justice's judgment of 5 november 2002 condemning eight member states for having concluded 'open skies' agreements with the united states, that the european commission present as soon as possible a communication on the future development of bilateral air transport agreements. as regards the union's external policy, we call on the commission to publish a green paper on the new frontiers of the enlarged european union, which would be accompanied by reflections on relations with the new neighbours and the various partners. it is regrettable that there is no reference in the commission's legislative programme to the creation of a euro-mediterranean free trade area, nor to the creation of a euro-mediterranean parliamentary assembly. in the context of the discussions on the post-doha era, we ask the commission how it hopes to integrate the commitment of europe not as a group of 15 but as a group of 25. finally, the transatlantic dialogue must be strengthened in the spirit of sustainable and supportive development and, of course, the kyoto commitments must be respected. we welcome the proposal to propose seven thematic strategies as set out in the sixth environmental action programme, as well as proposals for an integrated product policy and a new chemicals strategy. in conclusion, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it seems important to initiate the reform of the staff regulations, to strengthen the independence of olaf and to publish the declaration of financial interest of the commissioners and directors-general on the internet. i am convinced, mr president, that this will help us to avoid an exponential increase in the number of instruments, a superposition of criteria and, finally, an overload of work in the field of transposition in order to ensure an optimal future for the enlarged union. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioners, ladies and gentlemen, i too do not see how anyone could oppose the commission's priorities. achieve enlargement, ensure stability and security, strongly support economic recovery and employment, contain globalisation and ensure that the benefits of globalisation are redistributed as widely as possible, taking into account kyoto, monterrey and johannesburg, including a knowledge society, the development of research with more funding and a better osmosis between science and society; who can be against these goals ? - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as every year, the reading of the commission's legislative programme for 2003 is dizzying, first of all because it measures the extent of the european union's areas of intervention. it is clear that, from revision to reform of the treaties, the member states have given up their most legitimate prerogatives to become nothing more than the local authorities of the future european superstate. the theoretical introduction of the principle of subsidiarity, which you say you are finally taking into account after ten years, does not in any way limit the union's legislative appetite. the other legitimate objectives, such as the desire to analyse the impact of community legislation or to codify existing legislation, can only be approved. we could even say: why didn't we do it earlier? in writing. - the authors of the resolutions take as their starting point the fact that concentration in the media has increased sharply. in search of the philosopher's stone that would preserve pluralism, everyone goes to the european commission with his own request. some suggested that a "broad consultation of professional organisations" should be organised. others argue that "the political, economic and legal implications of a european regulatory framework or other regulatory alternatives to safeguard freedom of expression and media pluralism should be considered". others suggested that "a directive should be drawn up setting limits on media ownership" or "proposed limits on the appropriate use of advertising resources to ensure free competition". all these are ridiculous proposals whose only function is to make it appear that the european parliament is a bulwark for democracy. most newspapers and some television channels are owned by media groups which are themselves owned by trusts which own companies in many other fields: vivendi, lagardère, bouygues and a few dozen others play a decisive economic and social role and are more powerful than the state and far more influential than the electorate. in the face of these powers, governments and european authorities have no choice but to bow down, to respect the speculative profits on the stock exchange and the secrecy of the boards of directors.
in writing. - since the helsinki council, the european union has pretended to regard turkey as a 'normal' candidate, of the same type as the others, and has turned a blind eye to the substantive problems posed by this candidacy. the brok report adds some ambiguity, since, after rejecting an amendment which would have confirmed turkey's status as a full candidate, it nevertheless asks the european council to 'advance the accession process'. we believe that it would be totally premature for the copenhagen council to set a date for the opening of accession negotiations with turkey. we believe that it would be equally premature to set a date for a future meeting when we would set the date for opening. we must not fall into the trap of pre-established timetables, which the eurocrats use with deftness, taking advantage of the weakness of the member states. the helsinki council made a serious mistake in 1999 by recognising turkey as a 'european' state capable of joining the union. in reality, turkey does not fall within the framework prescribed by article 49 teu for accessions. on the other hand, it would be perfectly suited to a renewed euro-mediterranean partnership.
in writing. - this report highlights the extraordinary work done by the democratic authorities of cyprus to implement the acquis communautaire in that country and thus to meet their commitments. however, if the reunification of the island is not considered a criterion for non-accession to the european union, which i welcome, the political and peaceful settlement remains a priority. turkey must therefore support efforts to reach a comprehensive settlement as soon as possible, in accordance with the resolutions adopted by the un security council. the european union must exert its full influence in this context. as regards turkey's possible accession to the european union, it should be remembered that the real question of europe's borders is still open. the european union should therefore create a space of privileged relations with our close neighbours: turkey, russia, the maghreb countries.
in writing. - the recitals conceal a disastrous overall record, marked for all the countries concerned by a widening of social and regional disparities, a massive increase in poverty and unemployment - only the latter point is noted. these regressions and their causes are totally hidden because it is intended to give the impression that the only problems encountered are those of the old regime or the misapplication of liberal recipes. the very nature of the policies imposed by the eu is at stake. we also reject the positive assessment expressed on the enlargement of nato. the enlargement of the eu is therefore presented as a hypocritical 'institutional advance' without social rights, without the development of common public goods and without real democratic choices. but this judgment concerns the whole of the european construction. the declarations about the 'historic' character of the continent's reorganization are not accompanied by the budgetary means and democratic procedures which would actually make it possible to build, at the continental level, an upward alignment of living standards and rights. we believe that it is up to the peoples of eastern europe to determine whether the deterioration of their situation can be better combated by remaining outside the union or by joining it. (explanation of vote abbreviated pursuant to rule 137 (1) of the rules of procedure)
in writing. - i voted in favour of the brok report as amended, despite its ambiguities on the question of turkey, to make clear the historical importance of the reunification of the european continent, even if under the name of enlargement it is undertaken too late and under very imperfect conditions. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. it is urgently necessary to recognize that the unfortunate decision of the european summit in helsinki, which granted turkey the same status as a candidate country as, for example, poland or hungary, is not based on any geographical, historical, cultural or legal basis. the copenhagen summit offers an opportunity to resolve an ambiguity which, if not removed, will poison the relations between the member states and turkey in a lasting and profound way. instead of directly or indirectly setting a date for the opening of meaningless accession negotiations, we should clearly place our relations with turkey in the framework of a euro-mediterranean partnership which would be given real political substance, rather than being confined to a mere platform promoting free trade.
in writing. - the report claims, in its explanatory statement, that the renewal of the sea grant is a necessity for the four french outermost regions already hit by particularly serious unemployment. but since the sea-grant has been in existence for a century and a half, it is right to believe that it does not protect workers against unemployment. it is actually an additional tax on consumption. so he's cutting into the budget of the poorest of the poor. and there is no mention of the fact that the revenue from the grant of the sea is used, in particular, to finance various social aid funds. it is the state's responsibility to ensure proper social protection. instead of forcing the poorest to pay taxes to finance the funds that are supposed to help them, and instead of pouring huge sums of money into subsidizing the employers in these areas, including the construction of yachts for the rich, it should spend that money on creating useful jobs in public services. we voted against this report.
in writing. - this report, which proposes to fight corruption, only illustrates your inability to do so. but how could it be otherwise ? you have made industrial and banking secrecy, business secrecy, the supreme law precisely to cover with a modest veil the thousand and one embezzlements, bribes, scams and other schemes, which allow to maximize profit and even to conceal the waste that your economic system represents for society. to claim to reconcile business secrecy and the fight against corruption is to try to solve the square of the circle. and then, how do we fight corruption in an economy that turns everything into a commodity and where everything is bought and sold, muscles and brains as well as consciences? we are voting against this report to show how empty it is.
in writing. - the reduction of certain vat rates may be advantageous to consumers. although the term 'labor-intensive services' is in fact a thinly disguised subsidy to employers in certain sectors, consumers do not always find any advantage in it, as we would like to believe. we are in favour of the complete abolition of vat, this unfair consumption tax, which affects even those whose wages or pensions are too low to be taxable. it is a highly unequal tax, since it applies the same rate to the rich who spend only a very small part of their income on consumption and to the poor whose meagre resources are barely enough for consumption. we abstained on this report.
in writing. - the report highlights the deterioration of the situation in the central and eastern european (ceec) candidate countries as a result of the 'painful adjustment process in the ceecs'. this finding, which concerns research alone, is indicative of a more general situation. the collapse of research, the public funding previously devoted to it, the paltry salaries of researchers leading to a "brain drain" both to the outside and to the inside (to survival activities): these are some of the milestones of this "transition to the market economy" with which the european authorities are replete. we are told that european programmes which are supposed to support research in these countries could help to remedy this backwardness. but the rapporteur does not really believe in this himself, because he sees stabilization only as a long-term process. until then, western european companies will be "doing their business". they benefit from qualified researchers who are paid even less than in the west and have little choice. this alone says a great deal about the nature and the actual social content of 'enlargement'. so the only reason why we are not voting against this report is that some of the programmes and funding it deals with, even if they are primarily intended to support western european industrialists, may perhaps help some eastern european researchers a little bit.
in writing. - the advertising of tobacco products - like the protection of nature and animal welfare - always generates a controversial and passionate debate. i congratulate the rapporteur on the quality of his amendments and on his attempt to calm things down. we support his report, which seeks to reconcile tobacco prevention, a public health priority as recommended by the who, with the possibility for member states to maintain their provisions on advertising, without hindering the functioning of the internal market and while preserving some prospects for tobacco farming, a sector with an uncertain future, which allows many small farms to maintain a fragile balance. five hundred european producers met here in strasbourg from 5 to 7 november to express their concerns about the future of the cmu, which was set up in 1999, and to present the progress made. they have made a great effort to improve the quality of a production which represents only 6% of world production by reducing the tar in the plant (it should be noted that tobacco from virginia, which is increasingly cultivated, releases virtually no nitrates). let us support the efforts of the tobacco farmers!
in writing. - tobacco kills more people every day, and more than 500,000 europeans die each year from smoking or from exposure to secondhand smoke. in view of this scourge, the necessary measures must be taken, including a sharp reduction in any form of advertising or sponsorship of these products. we know that these communication actions contribute to the development of tobacco use, especially among young people. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. the amendments proposed by parliament are very ambiguous and do not take a position in favour of public health, quite the contrary. the drafting of the parliamentary proposals, which is covered by arguments misused in this context, in particular the emphasis on freedom of expression, leaves too much room for interpretation and does not contain a firm provision to protect europeans. let's not be hypocritical. communication on tobacco should be more focused on the dangers of tobacco consumption, which is very harmful to people and particularly costly for society as a whole.
in writing. - tobacco kills: five million people a year, 550,000 of them in europe, that's enough! the fifteen are in the process of adopting legislation to ban all tobacco advertising. we are in favour of this initiative, whose primary mission must be to protect public health. the advertising and aggressive marketing of tobacco targets our children first. according to who, 80 percent of the world's 1.2 billion smokers began smoking before the age of 18. so we must stop these direct and indirect incentives to addiction, disease and death. apart from two omissions, this proposal for a directive is a step in the right direction. firstly, it does not condemn indirect advertising, that is to say, advertising not on tobacco products but on the brand. the promotion of a brand, a symbol of the tobacco industry, obviously produces the same effects on consumption as direct advertising for a pack of cigarettes. secondly, this proposal for a directive creates a ceiling for advertising bans and not a floor as we would like. national legislation must be able to be more restrictive than the directive in this area. the introduction of a safeguard clause is therefore necessary. we shall vote on this text only if these two shortcomings are remedied.
in writing. - the commission's proposal to implement a multiannual programme of energy actions for the years 2003 to 2006 aims to strengthen community support in energy fields which contribute to sustainable development. this programme will replace the altener, save and partly synergie programmes, but will resume their activities. it will be organised around four themes: improving energy efficiency and demand management, particularly in the building and industrial sectors (save); promoting new and renewable energy for centralised and decentralised production and its integration into the urban environment (alterner); supporting initiatives on the energy aspects of transport, fuel diversification and the promotion of fuels of renewable origin, including energy efficiency in transport (steer); finally, support for initiatives to promote renewable energy and energy efficiency in countries through the development of the field (coopener). energy is a major concern in the union and i am pleased to see all these actions being brought together in one programme. improved efficiency in management and implementation can be expected. i also agree with the rapporteur that an increase in the budget is necessary if we are to be able to achieve our ambitions!
in writing. - the rapporteur notes that for more than twenty years the european institutions have been discussing how to combat organised crime (money laundering, drug trafficking, arms, human trafficking, etc.), but the measures taken - where they have been adopted - have been met with the member states' lack of cooperation or have remained without practical consequences, if not dead letter. and there is every reason to believe that the danish initiative will not fail to meet this requirement. and for good reason. the capitalist system is inseparable from organized crime, even in the sense of bourgeois justice. you mean the drug money? but in france and britain, how many so-called respectable fortunes date back to the time when the gunboats of these countries forced china to open up to the opium of the english and french colonies! and today, european banks are still making huge profits from drug, arms and human trafficking. in the face of this, the "small measures" we are discussing here, and which we abstain from, are paltry in their attempt to moralize a system that is deeply amoral and inhuman.
in writing. - this report states that it is concerned with fisheries in three aspects: environmental, social and economic, in the european union but also in its relations with countries, especially those of the third world. the rapporteur opposes the technical solutions to the current problems in fisheries, which he says are intended to mitigate the effect of 'liberalisation' policies in this area. we voted on the points in the report which seemed to us to be in the interests of small fishermen or consumers or in the interests of protecting the marine environment, but we abstained on the whole report. the report does indeed point to certain aspects which threaten the balance between man and nature and which also threaten the people who live off the sea, since they have no other resources, but it does not in any way call into question the logic of a social organization in which producers, workers and nature are always sacrificed on the altar of capitalist profit.
in writing. - the commission, under the guise of protecting the environment, is proposing to reduce the fishing fleet and in fact to favour the most powerful gear at the expense of the others, and thus to reduce the number of small fishermen. to save marine life, we should limit the harvesting, so what is the fishing? but it is not the predatory industrial fisheries that will be the victims of the proposed measures. nothing would prevent - and the rapporteur does not even for a moment envisage - the maintenance or even the improvement of the incomes of small fishermen, who are the only ones who make a living from fishing. this would be the only way to truly respect both the environment and the workers of the sea. instead, the report suggests that, among other things, they should be recycled into marine litter by using their boats to sweep up the black tides. and the worst part is that, unfortunately, this is an activity with a promising future given the behaviour of the big oil groups, the shipowners and their shareholders, and given the inability of the european and national authorities to make the collective interest prevail over the destructive selfishness of the capitalists. we therefore vote in favour of certain points in the report which would be in the interests of fishermen and the environment, but we abstain on the whole of the text.
- at its sitting on 24 october 2002, parliament gave its opinion on draft amendment no 654 to budget line b3/300 entitled 'general information measures on the european union'. the vote was as follows. the whole text except the pre-allocation for euronews and the reservations: this part is adopted; 2. a pre-allocation of eur 3 million for euronews by rolling call: this part is also adopted; 3. reservations for the pre-allocation of euronews: this part is rejected; general reservations: this part is adopted. the result of the vote was therefore: the pre-allocation of eur 3 million for euronews is maintained, the reserve for euronews is deleted, the appropriations are entered on the line and, finally, the overall reserve is maintained. amendment no 736 which was published in the annex to the minutes of the sitting of 24 october 2002 did not reflect the result of the vote in plenary, as the last two parts of the vote were reversed. the competent departments therefore made the necessary amendment.

- mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the chechen terrorists had a very bad idea when they attacked the moscow theatre. firstly, because the human toll is exceptionally heavy and my group, of course, bows to all the victims, whoever they may be. but this hostage situation has also blurred the lines of reference of our parliament. before september 11, the situation was simple: on the one hand, there was a people fighting for their freedom, for their right to self-determination - the chechens - and on the other, the tyrannical russian regime. finally, there were the americans, who also supported the cause of the chechen muslims out of self-interest. today, the investigation since the attack and its repression reveals that there are more than close links between the chechen movement and international islamic terrorism. chechnya has become a base for international terrorism, arms trafficking and drug trafficking. i ask you, ladies and gentlemen, not to repeat the mistake made during the kosovo war, when we followed the american media and communications fashion and applauded the bombing of serbian christians who were threatening the brave muslims of kosovo. since then we have seen, and we french in particular, that kosovo has become not only a transit route but also a base for islamist terrorists operating in western europe and, particularly, in france and germany. recent arrests in france, germany and, more recently, belgium bear witness to this. i therefore ask you not to make the same mistake with the chechen movement and to stand in solidarity with islamist terrorism. my group is of course in favour of russia, a country with a christian tradition and culture, joining the european union. history, geography, customs and traditions make it a perfect fit for the union, to which it would bring much richness and renewal. i think we should help it to move more and more towards democracy and human rights.

president of the council. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i am very pleased to have this opportunity to discuss the extension of the lamfalussy procedure to the whole financial sector. i very much appreciate the opportunity to present the council's proposal to the european parliament so that we can have a constructive and open dialogue between the council and the european parliament on this important subject. the committee on economic and monetary affairs of the european parliament has raised some questions concerning the restructured fspg and the participation of the european parliament in the discussions on financial policy. i hope that these questions can be resolved before the report is adopted by the ecofin council on 3 december. financial markets play an increasingly important role in europe's economy. they are an important factor in creating growth and jobs, and financial integration in the eu and the creation of a common market for financial services will make a significant contribution to increased prosperity. a report published by the commission last week shows that full financial integration in the eu would increase eu gdp by 1.1% in the long term. however, the increased financial integration also creates the need for improved cooperation on financial supervision in the eu and more attention to financial stability. the development of financial markets over the past year has underlined these needs. the ecofin council therefore wishes to extend the structure of financial regulation, supervision and stability of the securities market agreed by the european parliament, the council and the commission in february this year to cover the whole financial sector. the interinstitutional agreements concluded in connection with the securities markets will of course also apply in the extended structure. the monitoring of financial stability in the eu is also being strengthened. the use of this new structure is important and urgent for several reasons, including for the banking and insurance sectors: first, the new structure will contribute to financial stability and effective harmonisation of financial regulation by providing a framework for effective cooperation and convergence between financial supervisory authorities. the increasing integration and interplay of the financial markets in the eu makes this necessary and it must not be postponed. secondly, the circumstances which gave rise to the introduction of the lamfalussy procedure for the securities sector are also present in the banking and insurance sectors. we have today an inflexible, slow and heavy rule-making - and i am fully aware that the council can also be a retarding factor in the present process. we also have a disparate implementation of the common rules in the member states. the financial sector as a whole is developing rapidly and rapid and effective cooperation on regulation and supervision is as necessary for the other sectors as it was for the securities markets. the need to be able to react more quickly than the current structure allows. initiatives for new directives, such as the implementation of capital requirements in the banking sector and solvency ii rules in the insurance sector, will require some technical regulation at a retail level and it is therefore appropriate to use a more efficient legislative procedure in this area, similar to that for the securities market. the new structure will make a better distinction between what is at the core, that is, the political centre, and what can be left to implementing provisions which can be continually adjusted to the changing market conditions. although the commission is not expected to present its proposal for basel ii until spring 2004, it will nevertheless be useful for the new structure to be in place early. thirdly, the new structure is necessary to ensure the efficiency of the future enlargement of the union. the new structure is more operational and efficient in an eu of 25 member states. the advisory committee on banking, which currently carries out both level 2 and level 3 tasks, has 3 members from each country (i.e. one from the ministry, one from the supervisory board and one from the central bank). after enlargement, it will consist of 75 members plus a number of observers. the coordination and convergence of european supervisory practices can best be promoted by establishing a uniform structure for all sectors. the structure of the securities market is a suitable model for this. the new supervisory structure takes account of the fact that the organisation of supervision remains a national concern and creates a more transparent committee structure without mixed mandates, as is the case in the banking and insurance sector today. a firm and clear structure for cooperation across the different supervisory committees and for the relationship between supervisory committees and 'level 2' committees is established. this also establishes good supervisory cooperation across sectors and creates a clear and good division of responsibilities. the new structure therefore has the following overarching significance: it focuses more on the political issues - and thus on the general principles of the rules. the political and technical discussions are initially held in separate forums and the process is accelerated by the possibility of working in parallel at the technical level. greater transparency and engagement with the financial sectors in many countries is being achieved, and the implementation of the rules of the individual directives in each country is becoming more uniform, which forms the basis for more uniform supervision. finally, it will bring about greater coherence between the rules of the various parts of the financial sector. it is necessary to find a good structure for the role of the european parliament in the formulation of the general guidelines of financial policy, and i am convinced that this will also be possible. as a starting point, i envisage regular meetings between the president of the restructured fspg, the commission and the european parliament to strengthen the dialogue on the broad guidelines of financial policy. however, it is also possible to envisage a revival of the 2005 group, if that is preferable, as mentioned in the european parliament's resolution on this subject. as regards the restructured fspg and its role in the formulation of financial policy, we will take account of the concerns of the european parliament. the commission notes that the restructuring plan for fspg was submitted by the french authorities on 29 june 2013. the restructured fspg, on the other hand, will provide an overview and advice to the council and the commission. this will be reflected in the final report to be adopted on 3 december. the council notes that the european parliament considers it essential for the new structure to enter into force that the legislative system in the eu be amended so that a clear distinction is made between primary and secondary acts and that the necessary revocation clauses are in place. the council is aware that the commission intends to propose to the convention that article 202 of the treaty be amended to take account of the powers of the legislative institutions - the european parliament and the council. as you know, the council as an institution cannot take decisions which bind the convention or the forthcoming intergovernmental conference. this is a matter for the member states alone, which will define their own position in the convention and the intergovernmental conference. as president of the ecofin council, i can assure you that i can and will encourage my colleagues to draw the attention of their heads of state or government to the importance of this subject and at the same time to encourage them to consider and discuss this subject in the run-up to the intergovernmental conference. we in the council are aware that the role of the european parliament must be respected. it is very important that the convention and the intergovernmental conference consider a legislative system which allows for greater efficiency in the legislative process and respects the principle of subsidiarity and the powers of the institutions involved. it is necessary to find a solution both to the challenges facing the financial sectors and to the challenges facing the community as a whole. we must all be aware, however, that this is a cross-cutting issue which does not concern financial legislation alone. finally, may i express the hope that the final position of the european parliament on this matter will take account of the actual possibilities available to the council and the pledge of goodwill which i have given to the european parliament today.
commission. – mr president, this debate concerns both the resolution introduced by mrs randzio-plath and the report prepared by mrs van den burg. with your agreement, i shall first speak on the subject of the resolution and then come to the report produced by mrs van den burg. as you may know, the ecofin council has broadly endorsed the efc reports on extending the lamfalussy arrangements to insurance, banking and financial conglomerates. at the request of the council and the presidency, the commission has organised a public consultation which ended last week. overall the response of market practitioners, consumers and other interested parties has been supportive. we shall shortly make those responses available on our website, which is consistent with the open and transparent approach that parliament wishes to be applied to the whole lamfalussy procedure. the commission supports the council in extending the lamfalussy arrangements, fully respecting all aspects of our arrangements with parliaments and our agreement with this house. i believe it will, in time, bring real benefits as the legislative process becomes faster, more flexible and more transparent. let us remember what we are trying to do. one of our aims is to encourage the convergence of regulatory structures which, for securities, is now beginning to happen. we strongly believe that this is needed in the other sectors as well. i acknowledge your concerns about the lack of experience with the lamfalussy approach hitherto. inevitably this is a learning-by-doing process. we must examine any shortcomings, a task which has been specifically assigned to the interinstitutional monitoring group. but we still have to prepare, in time, for the decisions ahead, not least because we need time to put in place the framework and the structures to extend lamfalussy. moreover, whether or not we extend that process will also shape the type of directives we introduce in relation to banking, insurance and conglomerates. we must also take into account the need to establish efficient decision-taking structures before enlargement. we should not wait, therefore, until the year 2006 and beyond. having said that, i fully understand the arguments put forward by this parliament concerning the need for proper democratic and accountable standards and safeguards. the efc's proposals have benefited significantly from the input of my services. in particular they respect existing interinstitutional political and legal agreements and the prerogatives of this parliament. we have insisted on this throughout, as well as urging that the proposal should be submitted to public consultation. incidentally, i do not accept that handing over chairmanship of the financial services policy group to a member state will weaken the commission's role. the fspg will have a forward-looking prospective and strategic role but the commission's right of initiative and indeed its role in the comitology procedure will not be compromised. that is explicitly stated in the efc's report. i have noted parliament's continuing interest in participating in the fspg. but i should also like to note that the role of the fspg is to advise the council and the commission. it is not an interinstitutional group. however, we have the 2005 group – the president of the council referred to that – within which the three institutions could regularly discuss strategic issues. i have also noted parliament's call for a clear and unequivocal commitment to reform article 202 of the treaty. as you know, the commission has repeatedly stated that it supports the amendment of this article. president prodi said just that in this house on 5 february 2002, when we agreed with parliament the democratic safeguards for moving forward with the lamfalussy procedure. it is also in the commission's governance white paper, in the commission's communication on better regulation and in the commission's contribution to the convention, its communication of 22 may entitled 'a project for the european union'. in all those documents you will find the same opinion expressed, namely that we support parliament in its wish to change article 202 of the treaty. the commission will shortly come forward, probably on 4 december, with its communication on institutional architecture. the content of that is yet to be finalised but i can say that we believe that both branches of the legislature – the council and parliament – must in future be treated in an equal manner as regards control of the commission and the whole comitology process. that is clear. what i would counsel against – and here i should like to end my comments on the resolution introduced by mrs randzio-plath – is the adoption of a resolution today which you know in advance is politically undeliverable by the member states. they cannot give their approval in advance of an intergovernmental conference that will not start until 2004. they cannot give their approval to a particular outcome. surely the reasonable course of action would be to ensure that these important issues are firmly on the igc agenda when it begins. turning to the van den burg report, the commission broadly welcomes this report. i should like to thank mrs van den burg for having produced a report which is indeed timely, given the current debate on extending the lamfalussy procedure, a debate which is under way in parliament, the council and, as a result of public consultation, also among more widely dispersed interest groups. in my view the report is very focused. it concentrates on the key developments in the financial sector such as the supervision of conglomerates, the globalisation of financial sector issues and responses to shortcomings in the american regulatory approach. it strikes a realistic note in recognising the different supervisory approaches adopted by member states. the report calls on the commission to act in a number of areas. some of those suggestions are either being addressed or are in the pipeline. let me mention four of them: firstly, a dialogue with associations representing the financial and consumer sectors; secondly, a dialogue with the united states; thirdly, sound regulatory and supervisory principles for the relevant authorities in the candidate countries; fourthly, impact assessments for new legislative proposals. the commission may decide not to take forward all the suggestions in the report but we will certainly give them due consideration. i am pleased to note that the report is supportive of the commission in a number of areas. for example, it reaffirms the commission's leading role in framing legislation, enshrined in the treaty as the right of initiative. indeed it is a monopoly of initiative. the report also endorses the commission's role as a fair power broker. it notes the important work the commission services are doing on creating an integrated financial market which, as mr pedersen said a little while ago, is vital to the european union's medium-term goal of creating the most competitive and dynamic knowledge-based economy by the year 2010.
- mr president, after the collapse and the profound dysfunctions of the world financial markets, it is imperative to build stronger european rules and common prudential supervision. is the lamfalussy method appropriate? does it need to be extended ? it is based on the distinction between framework legislation and secondary legislation. this is a sound principle, but it poses a fundamental problem for the exercise of democracy. parliament, as a co-legislator, must be placed on a strictly equal footing with the council and, on this basis, have a call-back power. that is why, like my colleagues, - the next item is the report (a5-0364/2002) by mrs van den burg, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy, on the 2001 annual report of the european investment bank (oj 2001 l 225, p. before i give the floor to the rapporteur, i should like to welcome the presence among us of mr maystadt, president of the european investment bank, who will be speaking shortly.
president of the european investment bank. - madam president, let me first of all say how much i appreciate the opportunity to continue the dialogue with the european parliament, especially at a time when your assembly is opening its doors to parliamentarians from states which will soon join the european union. two weeks ago, in vienna, at the annual forum of the european investment bank, president cox recalled the historic importance of enlargement and emphasized in particularly eloquent terms that this movement is the indispensable continuation of the work of peace and stability begun by the founders of the european construction. the european investment bank, which was set up by the treaty of rome to provide financial support for the european community's political objectives, is also making a modest contribution to the success of enlargement. the european investment bank, which already has a loan portfolio of some eur 18 billion in the region, making it by far the largest lender, will of course continue to support the investments needed in the future member states. three areas in particular are being addressed: infrastructure, especially in the areas of transport, energy and telecommunications; the environment, because the investment needs are enormous to comply with community standards; and foreign direct investment, because it is a particularly powerful lever in the catching-up process. the preparation of the applicant countries for membership is therefore one of the five priority areas approved by the eib's board of governors when, last june, it gave its approval to a 50% increase in the capital of the european investment bank. i will briefly recall the other four priorities. firstly, regional development, with the objective of devoting 70% of our direct loans and at least 50% of our global loans to projects in regions eligible for assistance from the structural funds. secondly, what we call the i2i programme (innovation 2000 initiative), which was implemented following the lisbon european council and which aims to encourage investments that can contribute to the transformation of the european economy into one based on knowledge and innovation. over €13 billion in loans have already been approved under this initiative. another priority is the protection and improvement of the environment, with the aim of devoting between a quarter and a third of our total lending each year to environmental projects. the fifth priority is our support for the european development aid policy, with the launch of two new facilities: the euro-mediterranean facility, which was decided by the barcelona council, and the new investment facility created by the cotonou agreement between the european union and the acp countries. having thus briefly recalled the five priority areas for the coming years, i would now like to try to give some answers to the various speakers, while confirming my availability to give more precise and complete answers at committee meetings. first of all, i would like to respond to your rapporteur, mrs van den burg, who has put a lot of effort into this excellent report. i should like to speak briefly about the issue which is close to his heart: the use of eib bonds by pension funds. in the united kingdom, pension funds have already subscribed to longterm eib bonds. we have not yet had the same success in the euro market, but we are looking for formulas that could be of greater interest to pension funds and insurance companies. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the future of the internal market. i think, however, that it would be dangerous to make the number of jobs created directly by a project the decisive criterion in deciding whether to finance it. i share some of the reservations expressed by mrs peijs in this respect. we believe that our projects should have a positive impact on the economy, through the chain of innovation-productivity-growth-employment, but that it would be dangerous to make too direct a link between the number of jobs created and the choice of this or that project. as regards the financing of smes, i would remind you that we finance small and mediumsized enterprises in two ways: on the one hand, by means of global loans, since half of our global loans go to small enterprises, and on the other hand, by means of the contribution of risk capital from the european investment fund. i will tell the commission, in response to a remark by commissioner monti echoing one of the recommendations in the report, that we are indeed considering adopting the commission's definition of small and mediumsized enterprises. but first we must solve a problem, and that is the problem of mediumsized enterprises. these may be considered too large to be included in global loans, but too small to benefit from direct loans. when we have found the appropriate form for mediumsized enterprises, we will be able to align ourselves with the commission's definition. as regards the important question of the control of the european investment bank, i would say that, of course, we are quite open to the control of the court of auditors in its area of competence. mr blak, i can assure you that the court of auditors has access to all the documents it wishes to obtain under the tripartite agreement concluded between the commission, the court of auditors and the european investment bank. this agreement is working to the satisfaction of all three parties. the president of the court of auditors has confirmed this to me and you have just heard commissioner monti say that the commission is also satisfied with this agreement, which will be discussed again and renewed. so there is no problem in that respect. the court of auditors has the power to control the use of community funds and, in so far as the eib uses community funds, it is obvious that the court of auditors must be able to exercise its full control. but there is a whole sector of the eib's activities which has nothing to do with community funds, which are financed by funds which we raise on the financial markets all over the world. of course, these activities also need to be monitored. it is in our interest to be effectively audited, and we are already being audited by an audit committee and external auditors who report directly to the governors. that said, i think it would be very desirable to find a form of supervision that is appropriate for a bank. i have already said this before this house and i confirm it today. we are quite open to the idea, and even willing to be subject to some form of banking supervision. that is why we are following with great interest the discussions currently taking place on the possible creation of a european banking supervisor. mrs lucas raised some interesting questions, but i have already exceeded my speaking time. i can give her more information in committee, particularly on the lesotho project she mentioned. i can simply confirm that as soon as we became aware of indications of possible fraud, we ordered a thorough audit and we communicated the information gathered during this audit to olaf, the monitoring instrument you know, and to the lesotho judicial institutions. we have not found any fraud in the use of eib funds, but our investigation into this matter has revealed other elements which we have communicated to the competent authorities. i can tell you more about that in committee. i hope that these few points will help to clarify the situation and give you an idea of how we, together with all the bank's staff, envisage our mission and how we intend to carry it out in the coming years, in close cooperation with the commission and in dialogue with parliament.

- the agenda calls for the following reports to be discussed jointly: - report (a5-0352/2002) by mr lipietz, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the commission report 'xxxi report on competition policy 2001' (sec{2002) 0462 - c5-0282/2002 - 2002/2142{cos) ] - report (a5-0353/2002) by mr herzog, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the 2001 state aid scoreboard (updated spring 2002) (cos) [2001/2196{ini) ].
the commission madam president, i shall try to deal with a number of points in the short time available, since there are two reports. first of all, i would like to thank the rapporteurs, mr herzog and mr lipietz, for their excellent reports. both reflect once again the general support of this parliament for european competition policy, which is so important for the commission and its services. let me explain the main lines of our competition policy in the field of state aid. in this area, the commission continued its efforts to simplify, modernise and clarify the rules and practice. new disciplines and new community guidelines have been drawn up: for example, the adoption earlier this year of a new multisectoral framework sets out a much clearer set of rules for the assessment of regional state aid for large investment projects. another important example concerns the use of block exemptions, which allow member states to grant aid without prior notification. the block exemptions for small and medium-sized enterprises and for training have been adopted, and recently also the exemption for employment aid. as regards the reduction and reorientation of state aid, in the conclusions of the stockholm and barcelona european councils member states committed themselves to reducing the levels of aid. we have indeed seen a clear downward trend, but it is undeniable that the cumulative effect of eur 82 billion of aid continues to cause a significant distortion of competition in the union. let me now return to some of the issues raised in mr herzog's report. i am firmly convinced that the best way to promote the overall competitiveness of the community industry is precisely to maintain a firm state aid policy. state aid policy is sometimes criticised as being in conflict with measures pursuing certain community objectives. i think that in most cases this conflict is more apparent than real. the purpose of state aid control is to ensure that the positive effects of a particular measure are not undermined by the distortion of competition which the measure itself creates. i also share the view expressed in the report that more attention needs to be devoted to assessing the efficiency and effectiveness of aid. this is an aspect of aid policy for which the member states are primarily responsible. they must develop the evaluation of aid schemes, and the commission, for its part, intends to facilitate these processes by providing a forum for the exchange of experience. in the field of antitrust, the work was marked by our debate on the commission's proposal to modernise its procedural rules. the work in the council on the commission proposal - a proposal which has the broad support of this parliament, which i thank again - is now drawing to a close. the council is expected to agree the text of a new regulation next week. i am convinced that we will also see a considerable improvement in our procedures as regards the aspect which was most emphasized by parliament in its resolution, namely that european competition rules are applied in all cases which may affect trade between member states. the modernisation of regulation no 17, ladies and gentlemen, is an example of the permanent culture of reform which the commission is trying to encourage in itself and which, as we shall see shortly, also applies to mergers. i would also like to point out that the commission took the initiative in modernising the antitrust rules three years ago. you will also remember that it was not so easy, at the beginning, to persuade the member states that it would be in the interest of better european governance to have more decentralisation in this area. in the merger field, the number and complexity of proceedings which reach the second stage has increased rapidly. in 2001, the commission adopted five prohibition decisions. although this is the highest number of bans in a single year, it still represents only about 1.5% of all final decisions. in this context, it will probably not have escaped your attention that in october the court of first instance annulled two of these prohibition decisions, in schneider v legrand and tetra laval v sidel, in addition to the judgment in airtours v first choice, already mentioned in your report. a thorough discussion of the implications of these judgments for the work of the commission would require more time than we have at our disposal today. i would like to make a few comments, however. we are carefully evaluating the judgments, both to decide whether to appeal to the court of justice and to draw the necessary consequences for the future. however, we should not allow these specific, isolated incidents to distort our view of the community's merger control policy. as you know, we have been engaged in a wide-ranging reform of merger control procedures long before these recent judgments. if necessary, it may be appropriate to use the lessons of these judgments to implement even more radical reform than originally envisaged: that is precisely my intention, as i have already announced. apart from the question of whether or not we will bring an action before the court of justice, it is appropriate and incumbent on the commission to draw all the lessons it can from some of the assessments that have been made and the reform project will therefore be even more intensive and radical. i would like to make it very clear, however, that the improvement we are promising in the instrument will not mean a more condescending policy. we believe that merger control policy as well as competition policy in general must be fair and at the same time rigorous. i intend to propose to the college a radical reform of the merger control system by the end of december, of which i would like to briefly highlight some aspects. the first aspect concerns the timing of the survey. a major advantage of the european system, which is widely acknowledged, is the short time it takes. however, these rapid times also create certain inconveniences, which translate into nervousness, sometimes frantic, in the final interaction between the parties and the commission. we will not therefore renounce the advantages of this rapid pace of change - which is the case in europe, but not in the united states - but we will also propose to introduce a certain degree of flexibility with a number of provisions to suspend certain deadlines. other improvements to the decision-making process that i intend to propose include: formalising and extending the existing system of cross-checks in all cases that have reached the second stage; greater transparency, allowing access to the file and comparison of opposing market views at an earlier time than today; an increase in the human resources of the directorate-general for competition, both to operate more in line with the high standards set by the court and to strengthen the capacity for economic analysis. i would also like to deal very briefly with the question of judicial review in cases of mergers between undertakings, which i know is of great interest to the european parliament in general and to mr riis-jørgensen in particular. recent judgments have shown that the european courts carry out a meticulous and rigorous review of the substance of the commission's analysis in merger cases. the court of justice's review, which is rigorous and effective, should not only be effective in terms of substance but also in terms of timeliness. there is still a lot of room for improvement in the speed with which judgments are handed down. the fast track has already been introduced: we hope very much that the court of first instance will be able to speed up and increase the number of cases to which the accelerated procedure is applied. the commission is prepared - as we have already indicated - to strongly support the allocation of the additional resources which will undoubtedly be required by the court to implement these improvements. in addition, it may be useful to consider the appropriateness of specialised judicial panels dealing with certain categories of cases in the court of first instance or of a specialised merger division in the court of first instance. whatever reforms are considered for a winning system, it is important not to lose sight of the many merits inherent in our administrative system. i must say that, following the publication of the commission's green paper, very few voices have spoken in favour of abandoning or radically revising the present system. many companies, including many american companies, when faced with the choice between our system and the american system, indicated in the consultation that they preferred the european union system. and as you know, the systems based on administrative decisions in this area are certainly not exclusive to the commission. this is the model used at national level in most member states and reflects the european legal traditions. so what i'm going to propose are going to be significant improvements to the current system: in some ways, they will radically transform the current system. i am very much of the opinion that what we are proposing is the most modern and effective system of merger control, which will improve the european model by incorporating some aspects of the american model. for reasons of time, madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i shall not dwell on the other important points which have been raised in the two reports by mr lipietz and mr herzog. i shall not dwell too much on the subject which is also very dear to the chairman of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, mr randzio-plath, namely international cooperation, where decisive progress has been made over the past year.
the rapporteur. - mr president, i thank all the members who have supported me and particularly those who share the orientation of this report which i believe is balanced and concerned with reality. i note that the amendments by mr evans and mrs riis-jørgensen upset this balance and in fact condemn all state aid to market activities. i hope therefore that they will not be held back and that the balance achieved in the committee on economic and monetary affairs will be preserved in plenary. i have cooperated well with the competition directorate, which handles state aid policy very carefully and whose spirit of dialogue i greatly appreciate. as with all competition policy, state aid policy is facing new challenges. its primary objective remains to reduce all aid that distorts or threatens to distort competition, but other objectives must also be taken into account: competitiveness and growth - the lisbon objectives - and social cohesion, which implies support for the recovery and development of regions in difficulty. that is why the stockholm and lisbon european councils undertook to reduce not all aid but aid within the meaning of article 87, namely aid which creates unfair competition. they are calling for aid to be redirected towards horizontal objectives. all these council decisions must be implemented with firmness but also with discernment. i stress in my report that the effectiveness of horizontal aid must be assessed. for example, aid for research, the environment, training and employment is legitimate and often desirable. however, they are not always effective in relation to the lisbon and gothenburg objectives, and we will therefore have to make progress in our recommendations. it would also be dangerous to outlaw any notion of sectoral aid. the latter may prove indispensable for strategic projects in which europe is lagging behind and the market is failing, but also to cope with unfair competition on the world market, or to save production faced with very serious cyclical shocks. it is known that the commission itself has opened the debate on the link between competition policy and industrial policy. the enlargement of the union to include the countries of central and eastern europe also raises difficult problems which must be dealt with fairly. when the private sector does not want to finance the modernisation of the steel industry in poland or the czech republic, in a world context of overcapacity, should we ask these countries to give up the development of this sector? the steel aid must be reviewed. similarly, while it is legitimate to aim at the abolition of special tax schemes and their transformation into regional aid, it must not be forgotten that countries such as ireland have benefited greatly from them until recently and that the economic level of the eastern regions concerned is particularly low, so that the creation of viable enterprises will not happen spontaneously. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of a european network of national and regional authorities. the council and the commission are reassessing their interest in the community. in accordance with parliament's wishes, the court of justice recognised that financial compensation in return for the obligations imposed is not aid. we therefore hope that the commission will speed up its reflections on this basis and soon propose new tools to guarantee both free choice, the means of services of general interest and competition, and also to secure non-profit-making activities. finally, we ask the commission to speed up its work to consider the elimination of tax schemes described as unfair competition by the primarolo group as state aid. ladies and gentlemen, the scoreboard is a step forward in the direction of transparency and public debate, and we welcome it. however, the commission is aware of the limitations we have highlighted. the comparability of data between states is not ensured, the effectiveness of aid is not assessed and the comparison between the union and its major competitors in the world is not yet provided. these are all areas of work for the future, and it will be desirable to involve more civil society actors in these areas. let me say a word about competition policy as a whole. competition is essential for the sustainability and efficiency of the internal market. however, the european union has much to do in terms of industrial and technological development. there is no need to retreat in competition policy, but industrial and competitiveness policies must be brought to the same level in the treaties and in practice, otherwise the union will lag behind in terms of innovation, scale, networks and business creation. already, experts consider that its potential for growth in production and productivity has slowed down, even though we want to accelerate it. the merger procedure is only one aspect of the problem. we know that the general centralisation of powers within the dg is a problem, but it is not desirable to switch to the american model. in the reform being prepared, we prefer a much more open, deliberative and reasonable time-limits-compatible investigation procedure, while the decision would still be within the commission's competence.
mr president, the treaty on european union does not prohibit dominant positions, only their abuse. it does not provide for a system of prior approval of mergers. it follows that the creation of a dominant position following a merger operation must not be negotiated in advance with the commission and that such a dominant position is not in itself contrary to the treaty. here again, in order to exist, the commission has arrogated to itself powers it does not have, inventing for the purposes of the case completely arbitrary, even ridiculous criteria, when, for example, it analyses market shares country by country and product by product, while taking advantage of the frivolity, or even the absence, of the french authorities when it comes to defending french industrial interests. moreover, while the treaty establishing the european community does not in any way prohibit the development of state enterprises, the brussels commission is attacking french public enterprises as symbols, intolerable in its eyes, of triumphant colbertism. in this connection, any attempt to force the french government to privatise public sector enterprises will have to be met with a vigorous response by all employees or, why not, a general strike in all sectors of industry. it is not just the competition directorate that needs to be reformed, it is commissioner monti, who knows nothing about industry, who needs to be dismissed and the brussels commission put in its place.
- mr president, it is only in terms of free competition and free markets that any aid, whether it is state aid, european aid or local aid, distorts competition. i believe and say that this influence on competition is positive when it allows for spatial planning, efficient public services, a reduction in inequalities, better social management, long-term consideration and more research and development. in approving the approach of philippe herzog, whom i want to congratulate and support, i therefore confirm that state aid is necessary and justified, as he says, on at least two conditions: that it clearly and only meets the objectives set, in terms of amounts and duration, on the one hand, and that it is transparent, controlled and evaluated in its results, on the other.
